events.text: The existing coverage endpoint deliberately stops at residue-field lifts, so I’m checking the other legitimate route: characterize local surjectivity stalkwise on the big étale site. If Mathlib exposes enough geometric points, the finite-separable \(h^0>0\) lift may prove the agreed theorem without inventing a neighborhood-spreading theorem.

instance {F G : Sheaf J (Type w)} (f : F ⟶ G) :
    IsLocallySurjective (Sheaf.toImage f) := by
  dsimp [Sheaf.toImage]
  infer_instance

variable [J.HasSheafCompose (forget A)]

instance [IsLocallySurjective φ] :
    IsLocallySurjective ((sheafCompose J (forget A)).map φ) :=
  (Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff_whisker_forget J φ.hom).1 inferInstance

theorem isLocallySurjective_iff_isIso {F G : Sheaf J (Type w)} (f : F ⟶ G) :
    IsLocallySurjective f ↔ IsIso (Sheaf.imageι f) := by
  dsimp only [IsLocallySurjective]
  rw [Sheaf.imageι, Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff_range_sheafify_eq_top',
    Subfunctor.eq_top_iff_isIso]
  exact isIso_iff_of_reflects_iso (f := Sheaf.imageι f) (F := sheafToPresheaf J (Type w))

instance epi_of_isLocallySurjective' {F₁ F₂ : Sheaf J (Type w)} (φ : F₁ ⟶ F₂)
    [IsLocallySurjective φ] : Epi φ where
  left_cancellation {Z} f₁ f₂ h := by
    ext X x
    apply (((isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).1 Z.2).isSeparated _
      (Presheaf.imageSieve_mem J φ.hom x)).ext
    rintro Y f ⟨s : F₁.obj.obj (op Y), hs : φ.hom.app _ s = F₂.obj.map f.op x⟩
    dsimp
    have h₁ := ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (f₁.hom.naturality f.op) x
    have h₂ := ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (f₂.hom.naturality f.op) x
    dsimp at h₁ h₂
    rw [← h₁, ← h₂, ← hs]
    exact ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (congr_app ((sheafToPresheaf J _).congr_map h) (op Y)) s

instance epi_of_isLocallySurjective [IsLocallySurjective φ] : Epi φ :=
  (sheafCompose J (forget A)).epi_of_epi_map inferInstance

lemma isLocallySurjective_iff_epi {F G : Sheaf J (Type w)} (φ : F ⟶ G)
    [HasSheafify J (Type w)] :
    IsLocallySurjective φ ↔ Epi φ := by
  constructor
  · intro
    infer_instance
  · intro
    have := epi_of_epi_fac (Sheaf.toImage_ι φ)
    rw [isLocallySurjective_iff_isIso φ]
    apply isIso_of_mono_of_epi

end Sheaf

namespace Presieve.FamilyOfElements

variable {R R' : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w} (φ : R ⟶ R') {X : Cᵒᵖ} (r' : R'.obj X)

/-- Given a morphism `φ : R ⟶ R'` of presheaves of types and `r' : R'.obj X`,
this is the family of elements of `R` defined over the sieve `Presheaf.imageSieve φ r'`
which sends a map in this sieve to an arbitrary choice of a preimage of the
restriction of `r'`. -/
noncomputable def localPreimage :
    FamilyOfElements R (Presheaf.imageSieve φ r').arrows :=
  fun _ f hf => Presheaf.localPreimage φ r' f hf

lemma isAmalgamation_map_localPreimage :
    ((localPreimage φ r').map φ).IsAmalgamation r' :=
  fun _ f hf => (Presheaf.app_localPreimage φ r' f hf).symm

end Presieve.FamilyOfElements

/-!
# Points of a site

Let `C` be a category equipped with a Grothendieck topology `J`. In this file,
we define the notion of point of the site `(C, J)`, as a
structure `GrothendieckTopology.Point`. Such a `Φ : J.Point` consists
in a functor `Φ.fiber : C ⥤ Type w` such that the category `Φ.fiber.Elements`
is cofiltered (and initially small) and such that if `x : Φ.fiber.obj X`
and `R` is a covering sieve of `X`, then `x` belongs to the image
of some `y : Φ.fiber.obj Y` by a morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` which belongs to `R`.
(This definition is essentially the definition of a fiber functor on a site
from SGA 4 IV 6.3.)

The fact that `Φ.fiber.Elementsᵒᵖ` is filtered allows to define
`Φ.presheafFiber : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ A` by taking the filtering colimit
of the evaluation functors at `op X` when `(X : C, x : F.obj X)` varies in
`Φ.fiber.Elementsᵒᵖ`. We define `Φ.sheafFiber : Sheaf J A ⥤ A` as the
restriction of `Φ.presheafFiber` to the full subcategory of sheaves.

Under certain assumptions, we show that if `A` is concrete and
`P ⟶ Q` is a locally bijective morphism between presheaves,
then the induced morphism on fibers is a bijection. It follows
that not only `Φ.sheafFiber : Sheaf J A ⥤ A` is the restriction of
`Φ.presheafFiber` but it may also be thought as a localization
of this functor with respect to the class of morphisms `J.W`.
In particular, the fiber of a presheaf identifies to the fiber of
its associated sheaf.

Under suitable assumptions on the target category `A`, we show that
both `Φ.presheafFiber` and `Φ.sheafFiber` commute with finite limits
and with arbitrary colimits. (The commutation of `Φ.sheafFiber` with colimits
is obtained in the file `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Point/Skyscraper.lean`.)

-/

@[expose] public section

universe w' w v v' v'' u u' u''

namespace CategoryTheory

open Limits Opposite

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

namespace GrothendieckTopology

variable (J : GrothendieckTopology C)

/-- Given `J` a Grothendieck topology on a category `C`, a point of the site `(C, J)`
consists of a functor `fiber : C ⥤ Type w` such that the category `fiber.Elements`
is initially small (which allows defining the fiber functor on presheaves by
taking colimits) and cofiltered (so that the fiber functor on presheaves is exact),
and such that covering sieves induce jointly surjective maps on fibers (which
allows to show that the fibers of a presheaf and its associated sheaf are isomorphic). -/
structure Point where
  /-- the fiber functor on the underlying category of the site -/
  fiber : C ⥤ Type w
  isCofiltered : IsCofiltered fiber.Elements := by infer_instance
  initiallySmall : InitiallySmall.{w} fiber.Elements := by infer_instance
  jointly_surjective {X : C} (R : Sieve X) (h : R ∈ J X) (x : fiber.obj X) :
    ∃ (Y : C) (f : Y ⟶ X) (_ : R f) (y : fiber.obj Y), fiber.map f y = x

namespace Point

attribute [instance] initiallySmall isCofiltered

variable {J} (Φ : Point.{w} J) {A : Type u'} [Category.{v'} A]
  {B : Type u''} [Category.{v''} B]
  [HasColimitsOfSize.{w, w} A] [HasColimitsOfSize.{w, w} B]

instance : HasColimitsOfShape Φ.fiber.Elementsᵒᵖ A :=
  hasColimitsOfShape_of_finallySmall _ _

instance : IsSifted Φ.fiber.Elementsᵒᵖ := IsFiltered.isSifted

instance [LocallySmall.{w} C] [AB5OfSize.{w, w} A] [HasFiniteLimits A] :
    HasExactColimitsOfShape Φ.fiber.Elementsᵒᵖ A :=
  hasExactColimitsOfShape_of_final _
    (FinallySmall.fromFilteredFinalModel Φ.fiber.Elementsᵒᵖ)

/-- The fiber functor on categories of presheaves that is given by a point of a site. -/
noncomputable def presheafFiber : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ A :=
  (Functor.whiskeringLeft _ _ _).obj (CategoryOfElements.π Φ.fiber).op ⋙ colim

/-- Given a point `Φ` of a site `(C, J)`, `X : C` and `x : Φ.fiber.obj X`, this
is the canonical map `P.obj (op X) ⟶ Φ.presheafFiber.obj P`. -/
noncomputable def toPresheafFiber (X : C) (x : Φ.fiber.obj X) (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) :
    P.obj (op X) ⟶ Φ.presheafFiber.obj P :=
  colimit.ι ((CategoryOfElements.π Φ.fiber).op ⋙ P) (op ⟨X, x⟩)

@[ext]
lemma presheafFiber_hom_ext
    {P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} {T : A} {f g : Φ.presheafFiber.obj P ⟶ T}
    (h : ∀ (X : C) (x : Φ.fiber.obj X), Φ.toPresheafFiber X x P ≫ f =
      Φ.toPresheafFiber X x P ≫ g) : f = g :=
  colimit.hom_ext (by rintro ⟨⟨X, x⟩⟩; exact h X x)

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- Given a point `Φ` of a site `(C, J)`, `X : C` and `x : Φ.fiber.obj X`,
this is the map `P.obj (op X) ⟶ Φ.presheafFiber.obj P` for any `P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A`
as a natural transformation. -/
@[simps]
noncomputable def toPresheafFiberNatTrans (X : C) (x : Φ.fiber.obj X) :
    (evaluation Cᵒᵖ A).obj (op X) ⟶ Φ.presheafFiber where
  app := Φ.toPresheafFiber X x
  naturality _ _ f := by simp [presheafFiber, toPresheafFiber]

@[reassoc (attr := simp), elementwise (attr := simp)]
lemma toPresheafFiber_w {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : Φ.fiber.obj X) (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) :
    P.map f.op ≫ Φ.toPresheafFiber X x P =
      Φ.toPresheafFiber Y (Φ.fiber.map f x) P :=
  colimit.w ((CategoryOfElements.π Φ.fiber).op ⋙ P)
      (CategoryOfElements.homMk ⟨X, x⟩ ⟨Y, Φ.fiber.map f x⟩ f rfl).op

@[reassoc (attr := simp), elementwise (attr := simp)]
lemma toPresheafFiber_naturality {P Q : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} (g : P ⟶ Q) (X : C) (x : Φ.fiber.obj X) :
    Φ.toPresheafFiber X x P ≫ Φ.presheafFiber.map g =
      g.app (op X) ≫ Φ.toPresheafFiber X x Q :=
  ((Φ.toPresheafFiberNatTrans X x).naturality g).symm

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
/-- The (colimit) cocone which defines the fiber of a presheaf. -/
@[simps]
noncomputable def presheafFiberCocone (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) :
    Cocone ((CategoryOfElements.π Φ.fiber).op ⋙ P) where
  pt := Φ.presheafFiber.obj P
  ι.app x := Φ.toPresheafFiber x.unop.1 x.unop.2 P

/-- The cocone `Φ.presheafFiberCocone P` is a colimit. -/
noncomputable def isColimitPresheafFiberCocone (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) :
    IsColimit (Φ.presheafFiberCocone P) :=
  colimit.isColimit _

/-- The isomorphism `shrinkYoneda.{w} ⋙ Φ.presheafFiber ≅ Φ.fiber`. -/
noncomputable def shrinkYonedaCompPresheafFiberIso [LocallySmall.{w} C] :
    shrinkYoneda.{w} ⋙ Φ.presheafFiber ≅ Φ.fiber :=
  Functor.Elements.shrinkYonedaCompWhiskeringLeftObjπCompColimIso _

lemma shrinkYonedaCompPresheafFiberIso_inv_app_toPresheafFiber
    [LocallySmall.{w} C] {X : C} (x : Φ.fiber.obj X) :
    Φ.shrinkYonedaCompPresheafFiberIso.inv.app X x =
    Φ.toPresheafFiber X x (shrinkYoneda.{w}.obj X)
      (shrinkYonedaObjObjEquiv.symm (𝟙 X)) :=
  Functor.Elements.shrinkYonedaCompWhiskeringLeftObjπCompColimIso_inv_app_apply
    _ (Functor.elementsMk (Φ.fiber) _ x)

lemma presheafFiber_map_shrinkYoneda_map_shrinkYonedaCompPresheafFiberIso_inv_app
    [LocallySmall.{w} C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : Φ.fiber.obj X) :
    Φ.presheafFiber.map (shrinkYoneda.{w}.map f)
      (Φ.shrinkYonedaCompPresheafFiberIso.inv.app X x) =
    Φ.toPresheafFiber X x (shrinkYoneda.{w}.obj Y)
      (shrinkYonedaObjObjEquiv.symm f) := by
  rw [shrinkYonedaCompPresheafFiberIso_inv_app_toPresheafFiber]
  refine (Φ.toPresheafFiber_naturality_apply (shrinkYoneda.{w}.map f) _ x
    (shrinkYonedaObjObjEquiv.symm (𝟙 X))).trans (congr_arg _ ?_)
  simpa using shrinkYoneda_map_app_shrinkYonedaObjObjEquiv_symm.{w} (𝟙 _) f

section

variable {P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} {T : A}
  (φ : ∀ (X : C) (_ : Φ.fiber.obj X), P.obj (op X) ⟶ T)
  (hφ : ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : Φ.fiber.obj X),
    P.map f.op ≫ φ X x = φ Y (Φ.fiber.map f x) := by cat_disch)

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.privateInPublic true in
/-- Constructor for morphisms from the fiber of a presheaf. -/
noncomputable def presheafFiberDesc :
    Φ.presheafFiber.obj P ⟶ T :=
  colimit.desc _ (Cocone.mk _ { app x := φ x.unop.1 x.unop.2 })

set_option backward.privateInPublic true in
@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma toPresheafFiber_presheafFiberDesc (X : C) (x : Φ.fiber.obj X) :
    Φ.toPresheafFiber X x P ≫ Φ.presheafFiberDesc φ hφ = φ X x :=
  colimit.ι_desc _ _

end

variable {FC : A → A → Type*} {CC : A → Type w'}
  [∀ (X Y : A), FunLike (FC X Y) (CC X) (CC Y)]
  [ConcreteCategory.{w'} A FC]

section

variable {P Q : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A}

variable [PreservesFilteredColimitsOfSize.{w, w} (forget A)] [LocallySmall.{w} C]

instance : PreservesColimitsOfShape Φ.fiber.Elementsᵒᵖ (forget A) :=
  Functor.Final.preservesColimitsOfShape_of_final (FinallySmall.fromFilteredFinalModel.{w} _) _

lemma toPresheafFiber_jointly_surjective (p : ToType (Φ.presheafFiber.obj P)) :
    ∃ (X : C) (x : Φ.fiber.obj X) (z : ToType (P.obj (op X))),
      Φ.toPresheafFiber X x P z = p := by
  obtain ⟨⟨X, x⟩, z, rfl⟩ := Types.jointly_surjective_of_isColimit
    (isColimitOfPreserves (forget A)
      (colimit.isColimit ((CategoryOfElements.π Φ.fiber).op ⋙ P))) p
  exact ⟨X, x, z, rfl⟩

lemma toPresheafFiber_jointly_surjective₂ (p₁ p₂ : ToType (Φ.presheafFiber.obj P)) :
    ∃ (X : C) (x : Φ.fiber.obj X) (z₁ z₂ : ToType (P.obj (op X))),
      Φ.toPresheafFiber X x P z₁ = p₁ ∧ Φ.toPresheafFiber X x P z₂ = p₂ := by
  obtain ⟨⟨X, x⟩, z₁, z₂, rfl, rfl⟩ := Types.FilteredColimit.jointly_surjective_of_isColimit₂
    (isColimitOfPreserves (forget A)
      (colimit.isColimit ((CategoryOfElements.π Φ.fiber).op ⋙ P))) p₁ p₂
  exact ⟨X, x, z₁, z₂, rfl, rfl⟩

lemma toPresheafFiber_eq_iff' (X : C) (x : Φ.fiber.obj X) (z₁ z₂ : ToType (P.obj (op X))) :
    Φ.toPresheafFiber X x P z₁ = Φ.toPresheafFiber X x P z₂ ↔
      ∃ (Y : C) (f : Y ⟶ X) (y : Φ.fiber.obj Y), Φ.fiber.map f y = x ∧
        P.map f.op z₁ = P.map f.op z₂ := by
  refine ((colimit.isColimit ((CategoryOfElements.π Φ.fiber).op ⋙ P)).eq_iff' ..).trans ?_
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨⟨Y, y⟩, ⟨f, hf⟩, hf'⟩
    exact ⟨Y, f, y, hf, hf'⟩
  · rintro ⟨Y, f, y, hf, hf'⟩
    exact ⟨⟨Y, y⟩, ⟨f, hf⟩, hf'⟩

variable (f : P ⟶ Q)

lemma toPresheafFiber_map_surjective [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J f] :
    Function.Surjective (Φ.presheafFiber.map f) := by
  intro p
  obtain ⟨X, x, z, rfl⟩ := Φ.toPresheafFiber_jointly_surjective p
  obtain ⟨Y, g, ⟨t, ht⟩, y, rfl⟩ := Φ.jointly_surjective _ (Presheaf.imageSieve_mem J f z) x
  exact ⟨Φ.toPresheafFiber Y y P t, by simp [← toPresheafFiber_w, ← ht]⟩

lemma toPresheafFiber_map_injective [Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective J f] :
    Function.Injective (Φ.presheafFiber.map f) := by
  suffices ∀ (X : C) (x : Φ.fiber.obj X) (p₁ p₂ : ToType (P.obj (op X)))
      (hp : f.app _ p₁ = f.app _ p₂), Φ.toPresheafFiber X x P p₁ = Φ.toPresheafFiber X x P p₂ by
    rintro q₁ q₂ h
    obtain ⟨X, x, p₁, p₂, rfl, rfl⟩ := Φ.toPresheafFiber_jointly_surjective₂ q₁ q₂
    simp only [toPresheafFiber_naturality_apply, toPresheafFiber_eq_iff'] at h
    obtain ⟨Y, g, y, rfl, h⟩ := h
    simp only [← NatTrans.naturality_apply] at h
    simpa using this _ y _ _ h
  intro X x p₁ p₂ h
  obtain ⟨Y, g, hg, y, rfl⟩ := Φ.jointly_surjective _ (Presheaf.equalizerSieve_mem J f _ _ h) x
  simp_all [← toPresheafFiber_w_apply]

lemma toPresheafFiber_map_bijective
    [Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective J f] [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J f] :
    Function.Bijective (Φ.presheafFiber.map f) :=
  ⟨Φ.toPresheafFiber_map_injective f, Φ.toPresheafFiber_map_surjective f⟩

/-- See also the lemma `W_isInvertedBy_presheafFiber` in the file
`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Point/Basic.lean` which may apply
in more cases. -/
lemma W_isInvertedBy_presheafFiber'
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective A] [(forget A).ReflectsIsomorphisms] :

   148	    E.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
   149	  set F : Algebra.EtaleCover K := Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L with hF

   154	    (PicEtAff.mk_descentMap C g x).symm

   157	      (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toLinearEquiv

   159	  obtain ⟨Lc, hrig, hLcrep⟩ := relPic.exists_isRigidified_rep
   160	    (Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId K F.Carrier).restrictScalars k) ≫ σ)
   161	    (y : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))
   162	  have hmem : relPicMk C (overSpec k F.Carrier) Lc ∈ descentClasses C F := by
   163	    rw [hLcrep]
   164	    exact y.2

   166	  have hdesc0 := Over.IsRigidified.cechPicMap_doubleInl_eq_doubleInr σ hmem hrig
   167	  have hinl : doubleInl (k := k) F = tensorInl (k := k) (A := K) (B := F.Carrier) :=

   169	  have hinr : doubleInr (k := k) F = tensorInr (k := k) (A := K) (B := F.Carrier) :=

   177	  rw [hq]
   178	  refine congrArg (PicEtAff.mk C F) (Subtype.ext ?_)

   180	      (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) M) = (y : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))

   184	section-admitting field test** — étale separatedness (C1) plus effectivity (C2):
   185	`relPic C (Spec K) ≃* PicEtAff C K`. -/

   187	    relPic C (overSpec k K) ≃* PicEtAff C K :=

   189	    ⟨PicEtAff.unit_injective C K, PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section C K σ⟩

    15	
    16	The ONE fibre dictionary of the h¹-vanishing locus, and its openness on affine tests

    18	
    19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.IsH1VanishingAt` — the membership predicate in the

    23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picClass_divFamDivisor` — the missing class law of the field
    24	  dictionary's forward map: `𝒪(divFamDivisor G) = G.picClass`.
    25	* `DivFamZar.exists_effective_witness` — **(V1a) witness production**: at every field
    26	  `L` of the test, the fibre class has an effective witness of degree `n`
    27	  (`divFamDivisor` of a globally certified representative, via `DivFam.exists_toZar_eq`).
    28	* `DivFamZar.IsH1VanishingAt.subsingleton_of_picClass_eq` /

    32	  datum dictionary** (the heart of GAP-6): for a pinned cocycle datum over `S` and ANY
    33	  field `L` in a `k`/`S`-tower, `H¹(pair) ⊗[S] L` vanishes iff the mapped class has a

    35	  (`datumDiffBaseChange`) carries surjectivity of the base-changed Čech differential to

/-!
# Conservative families of points

Let `J` be a Grothendieck topology on a category `C`.
Let `P : ObjectProperty J.Point` be a family of points. We say that
`P` is a conservative family of points if the corresponding
fiber functors `Sheaf J (Type w) ⥤ Type w` jointly reflect
isomorphisms. Under suitable assumptions on the coefficient
category `A`, this implies that the fiber functors
`Sheaf J A ⥤ A` corresponding to the points in `P`
jointly reflect isomorphisms, epimorphisms and monomorphisms,
and they are also jointly faithful.

We provide a constructor `ObjectProperty.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints.mk'`
which allows to verify that a family of points is conservative
using a condition involving covering sieves (SGA 4 IV 6.5 (a)).

-/

public section

universe w w' v v' u u'

namespace CategoryTheory

open Limits Opposite

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  (P : ObjectProperty (GrothendieckTopology.Point.{w} J))

namespace ObjectProperty

/-- Let `P : ObjectProperty J.Point` a family of points of a
site `(C, J)`). We say that it is a conservative family of points
if the corresponding fiber functors `Sheaf J (Type w) ⥤ Type w`
jointly reflect isomorphisms. -/
@[stacks 00YK "(1)"]
structure IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints : Prop where
  jointlyReflectIsomorphisms_type :
    JointlyReflectIsomorphisms
      (fun (Φ : P.FullSubcategory) ↦ Φ.obj.sheafFiber (A := Type w))

namespace IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints

variable {P} (hP : P.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints)
  (A : Type u') [Category.{v'} A] [LocallySmall.{w} C]

section

variable
  [HasColimitsOfSize.{w, w} A]
  {FC : A → A → Type*} {CC : A → Type w}
  [∀ (X Y : A), FunLike (FC X Y) (CC X) (CC Y)]
  [ConcreteCategory.{w} A FC]
  [(forget A).ReflectsIsomorphisms]
  [PreservesFilteredColimitsOfSize.{w, w} (forget A)]
  [hJ : J.HasSheafCompose (forget A)]

include hP hJ in
@[stacks 00YK "(1)"]
lemma jointlyReflectIsomorphisms :
    JointlyReflectIsomorphisms
      (fun (Φ : P.FullSubcategory) ↦ Φ.obj.sheafFiber (A := A)) where
  isIso {K L} f _ := by
    rw [← isIso_iff_of_reflects_iso _ (sheafCompose J (forget A)),
      hP.jointlyReflectIsomorphisms_type.isIso_iff]
    exact fun Φ ↦ ((MorphismProperty.isomorphisms _).arrow_mk_iso_iff
      (((Functor.mapArrowFunctor _ _).mapIso
        (Φ.obj.sheafFiberCompIso (forget A))).app (Arrow.mk f))).2
          (inferInstanceAs (IsIso ((forget A).map (Φ.obj.sheafFiber.map f))))

include hP hJ in
@[stacks 00YL "(1)"]
lemma jointlyReflectMonomorphisms [AB5OfSize.{w, w} A] [HasFiniteLimits A] :
    JointlyReflectMonomorphisms
      (fun (Φ : P.FullSubcategory) ↦ Φ.obj.sheafFiber (A := A)) :=
  (hP.jointlyReflectIsomorphisms A).jointlyReflectMonomorphisms

include hP hJ in
@[stacks 00YL "(2)"]
lemma jointlyReflectEpimorphisms
    [HasWeakSheafify J A] [HasProducts.{w} A] :
    JointlyReflectEpimorphisms
      (fun (Φ : P.FullSubcategory) ↦ Φ.obj.sheafFiber (A := A)) :=
  (hP.jointlyReflectIsomorphisms A).jointlyReflectEpimorphisms

include hP hJ in
@[stacks 00YL "(3)"]
lemma jointlyFaithful [AB5OfSize.{w, w} A] [HasFiniteLimits A] :
    JointlyFaithful
      (fun (Φ : P.FullSubcategory) ↦ Φ.obj.sheafFiber (A := A)) :=
  (hP.jointlyReflectIsomorphisms A).jointlyFaithful

variable {A} in
include hP hJ in
lemma W_iff {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} (f : F ⟶ G) [HasWeakSheafify J A]
    [HasProducts.{w} A] :
    J.W f ↔ ∀ (Φ : P.FullSubcategory), IsIso (Φ.obj.presheafFiber.map f) := by
  rw [GrothendieckTopology.W_iff, (hP.jointlyReflectIsomorphisms A).isIso_iff]
  exact forall_congr'
    (fun Φ ↦ (MorphismProperty.isomorphisms A).arrow_mk_iso_iff
      (((Functor.mapArrowFunctor _ _).mapIso
        (Φ.obj.presheafToSheafCompSheafFiberIso A)).app (Arrow.mk f)))

omit [(forget A).ReflectsIsomorphisms] hJ in
include hP in
variable {A} in
lemma jointly_reflect_isLocallySurjective
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective (Type w)] [HasSheafify J (Type w)]
    {X Y : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : ∀ (Φ : P.FullSubcategory),
      Function.Surjective (Φ.obj.presheafFiber.map f)) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J f := by
  simp only [← ofHom_epi_iff_surjective] at hf
  rw [Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff_whisker_forget,
    ← Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_presheafToSheaf_map_iff,
    Sheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff_epi,
    (hP.jointlyReflectEpimorphisms (Type w)).epi_iff]
  exact fun Φ ↦ ((MorphismProperty.epimorphisms (Type w)).arrow_mk_iso_iff
    (((Functor.mapArrowFunctor _ _).mapIso
      ((Φ.obj.presheafFiberCompIso (forget A)).symm ≪≫
        Functor.isoWhiskerLeft _ (Φ.obj.presheafToSheafCompSheafFiberIso (Type w)).symm)).app
          (Arrow.mk f))).1 (hf Φ)

end

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
lemma jointly_reflect_ofArrows_mem
    [HasSheafify J (Type w)] [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective (Type w)]
    (hP : P.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints)
    {X : C} {ι : Type*} [Small.{w} ι] {U : ι → C} (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ X) :
    Sieve.ofArrows _ f ∈ J X ↔
      ∀ (Φ : P.FullSubcategory) (x : Φ.obj.fiber.obj X),
        ∃ (i : ι) (y : Φ.obj.fiber.obj (U i)), Φ.obj.fiber.map (f i) y = x := by
  refine ⟨fun hf Φ x ↦ ?_, fun hf ↦ ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨Z, _, ⟨_, p, _, ⟨i⟩, rfl⟩, z, rfl⟩ := Φ.obj.jointly_surjective _ hf x
    exact ⟨i, Φ.obj.fiber.map p z, by simp⟩
  · rw [J.ofArrows_mem_iff_isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_shrinkYoneda_map]
    refine hP.jointly_reflect_isLocallySurjective _ (fun Φ x ↦ ?_)
    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := (Φ.obj.shrinkYonedaCompPresheafFiberIso.app X).toEquiv.symm.surjective x
    obtain ⟨i, y, rfl⟩ := hf Φ x
    refine ⟨Φ.obj.presheafFiber.map (Sigma.ι (fun i ↦ shrinkYoneda.{w}.obj (U i)) i)
      (Φ.obj.shrinkYonedaCompPresheafFiberIso.inv.app _ y), ?_⟩
    have := ConcreteCategory.congr_hom
      (Φ.obj.shrinkYonedaCompPresheafFiberIso.inv.naturality (f i)) y
    dsimp at this ⊢
    rw [this, ← Sigma.ι_desc (fun i ↦ shrinkYoneda.{w}.map (f i)) i, Functor.map_comp]
    rfl

lemma jointly_reflect_ofArrows_mem_of_small
    [HasSheafify J (Type w)] [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective (Type w)]
    (hP : P.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints) [ObjectProperty.Small.{w} P]
    {X : C} {ι : Type*} {U : ι → C} (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ X) :
    Sieve.ofArrows _ f ∈ J X ↔
      ∀ (Φ : P.FullSubcategory) (x : Φ.obj.fiber.obj X),
        ∃ (i : ι) (y : Φ.obj.fiber.obj (U i)), Φ.obj.fiber.map (f i) y = x := by
  refine ⟨fun hf Φ x ↦ ?_, fun hf ↦ ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨Z, _, ⟨_, p, _, ⟨i⟩, rfl⟩, z, rfl⟩ := Φ.obj.jointly_surjective _ hf x
    exact ⟨i, Φ.obj.fiber.map p z, by simp⟩
  · let ι' : Type _ := Σ (Φ : P.FullSubcategory), Φ.obj.fiber.obj X
    choose i y hy using fun (j : ι') ↦ hf j.1 j.2
    refine J.superset_covering (S := Sieve.ofArrows _ (fun i' ↦ f (i i'))) ?_ ?_
    · rw [Sieve.generate_le_iff, Presieve.ofArrows_le_iff]
      exact fun _ ↦ Sieve.ofArrows_mk _ _ _
    · rw [hP.jointly_reflect_ofArrows_mem]
      exact fun Φ x ↦ ⟨_, _, hy ⟨Φ, x⟩⟩

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
private lemma mk'.isLocallySurjective
    (hP : ∀ ⦃X : C⦄ (S : Sieve X) (_ : ∀ (Φ : P.FullSubcategory) (x : Φ.obj.fiber.obj X),
      ∃ (Y : C) (g : Y ⟶ X) (_ : S g) (y : Φ.obj.fiber.obj Y), Φ.obj.fiber.map g y = x),
        S ∈ J X)
    {F₁ F₂ : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w} (f : F₁ ⟶ F₂) [Mono f]
    (hf : ∀ (Φ : P.FullSubcategory), Function.Surjective (Φ.obj.presheafFiber.map f)) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J f := by
  wlog hF₂ : ∃ (U : C), F₂ = shrinkYoneda.obj U generalizing F₁ F₂
  · refine ⟨fun {U} s ↦ ?_⟩
    let f' := pullback.snd f (shrinkYonedaEquiv.{w}.symm s)
    have hf' (Φ : P.FullSubcategory) :
        Function.Surjective (Φ.obj.presheafFiber.map f') := by
      replace hf := hf Φ
      rw [← CategoryTheory.epi_iff_surjective] at hf ⊢
      exact (MorphismProperty.epimorphisms _).of_isPullback
        ((IsPullback.of_hasPullback f (shrinkYonedaEquiv.{w}.symm s)).map
          Φ.obj.presheafFiber) (.infer_property _)
    have := this f' hf' ⟨_, rfl⟩
    refine J.superset_covering ?_
      (Presheaf.imageSieve_mem J f' (shrinkYonedaObjObjEquiv.symm (𝟙 U)))
    rintro V g ⟨v, hv⟩
    refine ⟨(pullback.fst f (shrinkYonedaEquiv.{w}.symm s)).app _ v, ?_⟩
    refine (ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (NatTrans.congr_app
      (pullback.condition (f := f)) (op V)) _).trans ?_
    dsimp at hv ⊢
    refine (congr_arg _ hv).trans ?_
    refine (congr_arg _ (shrinkYoneda_obj_map_shrinkYonedaObjObjEquiv_symm g.op (𝟙 _))).trans ?_
    simpa using shrinkYonedaEquiv_symm_app_shrinkYonedaObjObjEquiv_symm s g
  obtain ⟨U, rfl⟩ := hF₂
  suffices Presheaf.imageSieve f (shrinkYonedaObjObjEquiv.symm (𝟙 U)) ∈ J U from ⟨by
    intro V g
    obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := shrinkYonedaObjObjEquiv.symm.surjective g
    replace this := J.pullback_stable g this
    rw [Presheaf.pullback_imageSieve] at this
    have hg := shrinkYoneda_obj_map_shrinkYonedaObjObjEquiv_symm g.op (𝟙 _)
    simp only [Quiver.Hom.unop_op, Category.comp_id] at hg
    simpa [← hg]⟩
  refine hP _ (fun Φ u ↦ ?_)
  obtain ⟨x₁, hx₁⟩ := hf Φ (Φ.obj.shrinkYonedaCompPresheafFiberIso.inv.app _ u)
  obtain ⟨V, v, y, rfl⟩ := Φ.obj.toPresheafFiber_jointly_surjective (A := Type w) x₁
  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := shrinkYonedaObjObjEquiv.symm.surjective (f.app _ y)
  refine ⟨V, t, ⟨y, ht.symm.trans ?_⟩, v, ?_⟩
  · simpa using (shrinkYoneda_obj_map_shrinkYonedaObjObjEquiv_symm t.op (𝟙 _)).symm
  · refine (Φ.obj.shrinkYonedaCompPresheafFiberIso.symm.app U).toEquiv.injective ?_
    dsimp [-Functor.comp_obj]
    trans (Φ.obj.toPresheafFiber V v (shrinkYoneda.{w}.obj U)) (shrinkYonedaObjObjEquiv.symm t)
    · rw [← Φ.obj.presheafFiber_map_shrinkYoneda_map_shrinkYonedaCompPresheafFiberIso_inv_app]
      exact Φ.obj.shrinkYonedaCompPresheafFiberIso.inv.naturality_apply t v
    · rw [← hx₁]
      refine Eq.trans (congr_arg _ ht)
        (Φ.obj.toPresheafFiber_naturality_apply f _ v y).symm

/- Let `P` be family of points of a site `(C, J)`, we show that `P` is a conservative
family of points if the following condition is satisfied (SGA 4 IV 6.5 (a)):
for any sieve `S : Sieve X`, if the family of maps `Φ.map.fiber.map f`
for all morphisms `f` in the sieve `S` is jointly surjective for any `Φ` in `P`,
then `S` is a covering sieve for `J`. -/
lemma mk' [HasSheafify J (Type w)]
    (hP : ∀ ⦃X : C⦄ (S : Sieve X) (_ : ∀ (Φ : P.FullSubcategory) (x : Φ.obj.fiber.obj X),
      ∃ (Y : C) (g : Y ⟶ X) (_ : S g) (y : Φ.obj.fiber.obj Y), Φ.obj.fiber.map g y = x),
        S ∈ J X) :
    P.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints where
  jointlyReflectIsomorphisms_type :=
    JointlyFaithful.jointlyReflectsIsomorphisms
      (JointlyFaithful.of_jointly_reflects_isIso_of_mono (fun _ _ f _ hf ↦ by
        have : Epi f := by
          rw [← Sheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff_epi]
          exact mk'.isLocallySurjective hP _
            (fun Φ ↦ ((isIso_iff_bijective _).1 (hf Φ)).2)
        exact Balanced.isIso_of_mono_of_epi f))

end IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints

end ObjectProperty

namespace GrothendieckTopology

/-- A site has enough points (relatively to a universe `w`)
if it has a `w`-small conservative family of points. -/
class HasEnoughPoints (J : GrothendieckTopology C) : Prop where
  exists_objectProperty (J) :
    ∃ (P : ObjectProperty (Point.{w} J)),
      ObjectProperty.Small.{w} P ∧ P.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints

end GrothendieckTopology

end CategoryTheory

events.text: The available machinery is richer than the field-level coverage theorem suggests: there are dedicated datum extraction, base-change, projective-H0, and section-cutting modules.    143	`p` (rank `1`, fibrewise nonzero), any second element `q'` lies in the `B_f`-span of `q`,
   144	so `q'` equals `a • q` in the away localization `Q_f` for a scalar `a : Localization.Away f`.

   146	Zariski-locally, by a scalar rescaling — and, when `q'` is itself fibrewise nonzero, by a
   147	**unit** rescaling (a `DivEq` move). -/
   148	theorem exists_notMem_smul_eq_of_tmul_ne_zero
   149	    [Module.Finite B Q] [Module.Projective B Q] (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
   150	    (hrank : Module.rankAtStalk Q p = 1) (q q' : Q)
   151	    (hq : (q ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) : Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
   152	    ∃ f : B, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ ∃ a : Localization.Away f,
   153	      (LocalizedModule.mk q' 1 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q) = a • LocalizedModule.mk q 1 := by
   154	  obtain ⟨f, hf, hbij⟩ := exists_notMem_bijective_toSpanSingleton p hrank q hq
   155	  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hbij.surjective (LocalizedModule.mk q' 1)
   156	  induction y using LocalizedModule.induction_on with
   157	  | h r s =>
   158	    refine ⟨f, hf, Localization.mk r s, ?_⟩
   159	    rw [← hy, LocalizedModule.mk_smul_mk, mul_one, LocalizedModule.map_mk,
   160	      LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply]
   161

     9	# THE PRODUCER: `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` for a class in the image of the sheafification unit
    10	
    11	## What this file closes
    12	
    13	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean` proves CHART-U(b) at a general test from a per-affine-piece
    14	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, and its header says plainly what it does not do:
    15	
    16	> The hypothesis is a *per-affine-piece existence of a datum with the plus-class property*, and
    17	> nothing here produces such a datum.
    18	
    19	**This file produces one**, and the ingredient that was missing is smaller than four successive
    20	sessions on this leaf priced it: on an **affine** test the canonical field point `Over.testPoint t`
    21	**is** the base-change morphism `overSpecMap A κ(t)`.  Both sides are `Spec` of the same ring map —
    22	`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine` is *defined* as `Spec.preimage` of `fromSpecResidueField`,
    23	so `Spec.map_preimage` closes it — but nothing in the tree said so, and every plus-class identity
    24	on this lane is an identity between a class pulled along `Over.testPoint` and one pulled along
    25	`relCurveMap`.  Without the comparison the two sides are not even syntactically comparable; with
    26	it they are the same class.
    27	
    28	## The shape of the producer, and its one genuine restriction
    29	
    30	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D` compares `μ`'s fibre at `κ(t)`, read as a plus class, with the
    31	plus-*unit* of `D`'s fibre class.  So the natural hypothesis on `μ` is that it is *already* a
    32	plus unit — i.e. in the image of the sheafification unit `relPicToPicEt` — and then `D` comes
    33	from `exists_cechPicClass_eq` applied to any Čech representative.
    34	
    35	That restriction is real and is named `IsPlusHonest` below.  It is **not** vacuous and **not**
    36	automatic:
    37	
    38	* not automatic — a general plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`,
    39	  and `Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is precisely the record that it becomes honest only over
    40	  `E.Carrier`, not over `A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is a genuine hypothesis, not a restatement;
    41	* not vacuous, and this is the payoff — the range of `relPicToPicEt` is a **subgroup**, and every
    42	  class the chart layer twists by is in it: the θ-family (`thetaFamily_isPlusHonest`), the
    43	  Σ-family, and the Abel value itself (`abelDiv_isPlusHonest`).  So `chartTwist` preserves
    44	  honesty, and CHART-U(b) becomes **unconditional** on exactly the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart reads.
    45	
    46	  **A CORRECTION TO THIS PARAGRAPH, from a fresh-context review of the commit that first wrote
    47	  it, and it is the same failure this leaf recorded one round earlier.**  When first committed the
    48	  sentence above cited `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` **and that declaration did not exist** — a
    49	  workspace-wide grep returned exactly one hit, the sentence itself.  That is precisely the
    50	  failure mode r7 diagnosed (`docstring-declaration-lists-unchecked`) and filed a lesson about,
    51	  reproduced by the very session that filed it, inside its own *non-vacuity* argument.
    52	  A kernel check, a `sorry` census and an axiom probe are all silent about it.
    53	
    54	  It also mattered mathematically, which is why it was worth writing rather than deleting: the
    55	  θ- and Σ-witnesses are the **twist factors**, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest` discharges anyway,
    56	  so they say nothing about the class being *charted*.  Since `chartValue = abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹`,
    57	  honesty of a chart value reduces to honesty of `abelDiv` alone — so `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` was
    58	  carrying the whole of the final clause.  It is now proved (below), so the paragraph stands as
    59	  written; had it not been, the honest statement would have been "no residue beyond
    60	  `IsPlusHonest lam`", with the Σ-chart clause unproved.
    61	
    62	## Main declarations
    63	
    64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.testPoint_eq_overSpecMap` — **the comparison**: on an affine test the
    65	  canonical field point is the base-change morphism.
    66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt` — the producer, with the datum given.
    67	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range` — **the producer proper**: for a
    68	  class in the image of the unit, a datum with the plus-class property EXISTS.
    69	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsPlusHonest` — the per-affine-piece form, closed under the group operations.
    70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest` — **CHART-U(b) with no residue** for an
    71	  honest class, and `chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest` the same open as DATA.
    72	-/

    99	
   100	/-- **On an affine test, the canonical field point is the base-change morphism.**

   102	`Over.testPoint t : overSpec k κ(t) ⟶ overSpec k A` is built from mathlib's
   103	`Scheme.fromSpecResidueField`, while `overSpecMap A κ(t)` is `Spec` of `algebraMap A κ(t)`.  They

   105	*defined* to be `Spec.preimage` of that very morphism, so `Spec.map_preimage` is the whole proof.

   108	`Over.testPoint` (the `chartLocus` side, indexed by points of a test) with one pulled along
   109	`relCurveMap C A κ(t)` (the datum side, indexed by base change).  Absent this lemma the two are

   112	sessions on this leaf priced the missing producer as the identification of a fibre class, i.e.
   113	as geometry, when what was missing was a comparison of two spellings of one morphism. -/
   114	theorem testPoint_eq_overSpecMap {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   115	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
   116	    Over.testPoint t
   117	      = overSpecMap (k := k) A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) := by
   118	  apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   119	  simp only [Over.testPoint_left, overSpecMap_left]
   120	  rw [Over.algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine]
   121	  exact (Spec.map_preimage _).symm

   127	theorem relCurveMap_testPoint {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]

   137	variable (C π) in
   138	/-- **THE PRODUCER, with the datum supplied**: if `μ` is the unit image of a relative Picard
   139	class presented by the Čech class `L₀`, then any datum whose class is `L₀` satisfies

   143	`κ(t)` inside the unit; `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt` collapses the affine comparison to
   144	`PicEtAff.unit`; `PicEtAff.map_id` deletes the identity restriction `κ(t) → κ(t)` that
   145	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`'s left-hand side carries; and `relCurveMap_testPoint` identifies

   154	about a fibre class would need the curve's geometry; this one needs the curve only to have the

   156	theorem isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]

   161	  intro t
   162	  rw [picEtMap_relPicToPicEt, picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt, PicEtAff.map_id, hD,

   168	/-- **THE PRODUCER PROPER**: for a class in the image of the sheafification unit, a datum with
   169	the plus-class property EXISTS.
   170	
   171	The datum comes from `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq` (the extraction keystone,
   172	`Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301`) applied to any Čech representative of the class, and

   174	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` asks for is met outright, with no choice left to the caller.

   177	too is `GeometricallyReduced`-free. -/
   178	theorem exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   179	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A))
   180	    (hμ : ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k A), relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A) z = μ) :
   181	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π, IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D := by
   182	  obtain ⟨z, rfl⟩ := hμ
   183	  obtain ⟨L₀, rfl⟩ := relPicMk_surjective C (overSpec k A) z
   184	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq
   185	    (C := C) (B := A) (π := π) L₀
   186	  exact ⟨D, isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt C π L₀ D hD⟩

   188	/-! ## The honesty hypothesis, and why it is not vacuous -/
   189	
   190	variable (C) in
   191	/-- **The honesty hypothesis: `μ` is a plus unit on every affine piece of the test.**
   192	
   193	This is the one thing the producer needs of `μ`, and it is a genuine hypothesis rather than a
   194	restatement: a plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`, and
   195	`Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is the record that it becomes honest over `E.Carrier` and not over

   200	def IsPlusHonest (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (μ : picEt C T) : Prop :=
   201	  ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens, ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)),

   252	    rw [picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt, thetaFamily_overSpec_affineEquiv])

   255	/-- A Σ-family is honest: it *is* a θ-family (`sigmaFamily` is defined as one). -/

   257	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
   258	    IsPlusHonest C T (sigmaFamily C Z T) :=
   259	  thetaFamily_isPlusHonest C _ T

   262	/-- **THE ABEL VALUE IS HONEST AT EVERY TEST** — the witness that carries weight, and the one this
   263	file's header cited by name before it existed (see the header's own retraction).
   264	
   265	The θ- and Σ-family witnesses above are the *twist factors*, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest`

   270	
   271	It is cheap for a structural reason: `abelDiv`'s components are `abelDivPlus`, i.e. `PicEtAff.unit`
   272	of `relPicMk` of the family's class, and `relPicToPicEt`'s components are `PicEtAff.unit` of
   273	`relPicMap` — so the witness on the piece `U` is the class of the *restricted* family, and
   274	`abelDiv_val` plus `picEtMap_abelDiv` line the two up. -/
   275	theorem abelDiv_isPlusHonest {n : ℕ} (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   276	    (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
   277	    IsPlusHonest C T (abelDiv C π n T s) := by
   278	  intro U
   279	  refine ⟨relPicMk C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1))
   280	    ((divFamZarAffineEquiv C π n Γ(T.left, U.1)
   281	      (divFamZar.map C π n (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) s)).picClass), ?_⟩

   294	theorem chartTwist_isPlusHonest (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)

   302	
   303	set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in

   305	/-- **CHART-U(b) AT A GENERAL TEST, WITH NO RESIDUE**, for a class that is honest on the affine

   308	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` needs a per-piece datum with the plus-class property;

    10	# Sections to divisors — the LocalEquations construction and the class law (DAT-A)
    11	
    12	Worksheet §2.2 step 2, made literal (`informal/spec-dat-a.md` §3): a global section of
    13	the DAT-1 glued sheaf **is** a matching family `(s_j)` with `s_i = g_{ij}·s_j`, so once
    14	its components are germ-regular (DAT-A2, `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionsToDivisors`)
    15	it is a `Scheme.LocalEquations` datum on the nose. The (1e) class law
    16	(`Cohomology/GluedSheafClass.lean`, landed while this brick was in flight) is consumed
    17	directly — the spec's `cocycleClassOn` seam is CLOSED, no interim class carrier exists:
    18	
    19	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionLocalEquations` — the LocalEquations datum of a
    20	  germ-regular global section on **any** pointed cover subordinated to the pieces
    21	  (the (1e) subordination interface `𝒲, σ, hσ`): equations the restricted components
    22	  `D.component s (σ y)`, ratio witnesses the subordinated transition units
    23	  `gluedSubordUnit`;
    24	* `sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit` — the ratio units are **exactly** the (restricted)
    25	  transition units of the cocycle (`ratioUnit_unique`); on the piece cover the
    26	  restriction is along `≤`-reflexivity, i.e. the units themselves;
    27	* `sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle` — the units cocycle of the constructed datum is
    28	  the (1e) subordinated cocycle `gluedSubordCocycle`;
    29	* **the class law** `sectionLocalEquations_picClass`:
    30	  `(D.sectionLocalEquations …).picClass = D.cechPicClass` — the divisor datum cut out
    31	  by a germ-regular section presents THE class of the datum's cocycle (the Abel
    32	  correspondence), through the landed `cechPicClass_eq_mk`. Naturality under
    33	  refinement/subordination-choice is the landed `gluedSubordCocycle_class_eq`; unit
    34	  rescalings and cover refinements of the constructed datum keep the class by the
    35	  landed `LocalEquations.picClass_rescale`/`picClass_restrict`;
    36	* `sectionLocalEquations_picClass_congr` — any two germ-regular sections on any two
    37	  subordinated covers cut divisors of the same class;
    38	* `sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular` — the A2-bundled wrapper on the canonical
    39	  pointed cover (`D.pointedCover`): a fibrewise-regular global section yields the
    40	  divisor datum outright, with class `D.cechPicClass` (`[IsNoetherianRing B]`).
    41	-/

    58	/-- The value of a restricted unit section is the restriction of its value. -/
    59	private lemma val_unitsRestrict {X : Scheme.{u}} {W U : X.Opens} (h : W ≤ U)
    60	    (u : Γ(X, U)ˣ) :
    61	    ((X.unitsRestrict h u : Γ(X, W)ˣ) : Γ(X, W)) = X.resHom h (u : Γ(X, U)) :=

    66	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
    67	variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
    68	variable (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
    69	variable (𝒲 : (relCurve C B).PointedCover) (σ : relCurve C B → D.index)
    70	variable (hσ : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ y))
    71	
    72	/-- The defining ratio equation of the section's restricted components on the overlaps
    73	of a subordinated pointed cover: the matching relation of the glued family, restricted
    74	from `⊤ ⊓ Uᵢ ⊓ Uⱼ`. -/
    75	private lemma component_ratio_eq (y y' : relCurve C B) :
    76	    ((relCurve C B).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
    77	        𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y' ≤ 𝒲.opens y)).op).hom
    78	        ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)))
    79	      = (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :
    80	            Γ(relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'))
    81	        * ((relCurve C B).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
    82	            𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y' ≤ 𝒲.opens y')).op).hom
    83	            ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y') (D.component s (σ y'))) := by
    84	  have hle : 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'
    85	      ≤ ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces (σ y) ⊓ D.pieces (σ y') :=
    86	    le_inf (le_inf le_top (inf_le_left.trans (hσ y))) (inf_le_right.trans (hσ y'))
    87	  have key := congrArg ((relCurve C B).resHom hle) (s.property (σ y) (σ y'))
    88	  rw [map_mul] at key
    89	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at key
    90	  change (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_left
    91	      ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)))
    92	    = (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :
    93	        Γ(relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'))
    94	      * (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_right
    95	          ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y') (D.component s (σ y')))
    96	  rw [gluedSubordUnit, val_unitsRestrict, component, component]
    97	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom]
    98	  exact key
    99	
   100	/-- **Sections ↦ divisor families** (DAT-A, worksheet §2.2 step 2): a germ-regular
   101	global section of the DAT-1 glued sheaf is a `Scheme.LocalEquations` datum on any
   102	pointed cover subordinated to the pieces — the equations are the (restricted)
   103	components, the ratio witnesses the subordinated transition units. Germ-regularity
   104	(`hreg`) is DAT-A2's output (`germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors` relatively;
   105	`Scheme.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero` on an integral field-level curve). -/
   106	noncomputable def sectionLocalEquations
   107	    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
   108	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
   109	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y)) :
   110	    (relCurve C B).LocalEquations where
   111	  cover := 𝒲
   112	  eqn y := (relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y))
   113	  regular y z hz := by
   114	    rw [Scheme.resHom, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
   115	    exact hreg (σ y) z (hσ y hz)
   116	  ratio_isUnit y y' :=
   117	    ⟨gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y', D.component_ratio_eq s 𝒲 σ hσ y y'⟩
   118	
   119	variable (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
   120	  ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
   121	    ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y))
   122	
   123	@[simp]
   124	lemma sectionLocalEquations_cover :
   125	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).cover = 𝒲 :=
   126	  rfl
   127	
   128	@[simp]
   129	lemma sectionLocalEquations_eqn (y : relCurve C B) :
   130	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).eqn y
   131	      = (relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)) :=
   132	  rfl
   133	
   134	/-- **The ratio units are exactly the cocycle's transition units** (worksheet §2.2 step
   135	2's "ratio units EXACTLY the cocycle"), in subordinated form: by uniqueness of ratio
   136	witnesses against a regular equation. On the piece cover the subordination is
   137	`≤`-reflexivity and `gluedSubordUnit` is the transition unit restricted along it. -/
   138	lemma sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit (y y' : relCurve C B) :
   139	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).ratioUnit y y'
   140	      = gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :=
   141	  ((D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).ratioUnit_unique y y'
   142	    (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y')
   143	    (D.component_ratio_eq s 𝒲 σ hσ y y')).symm
   144	
   145	/-- The units cocycle of the constructed LocalEquations datum is the (1e) subordinated
   146	cocycle of the datum. -/
   147	lemma sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle :
   148	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle
   149	      = gluedSubordCocycle D.isGluingCocycle 𝒲 σ hσ :=
   150	  Scheme.unitsCocycle_ext fun y y' =>
   151	    ((D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle_evInf y y').trans
   152	      ((D.sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg y y').trans
   153	        (gluedSubordCocycle_evInf D.isGluingCocycle 𝒲 σ hσ y y').symm)
   154	
   155	/-- **THE CLASS LAW** (DAT-A keystone; the Abel correspondence of worksheet §2.2 step
   156	2): the Picard class of the divisor datum cut out by a germ-regular global section of
   157	the DAT-1 glued sheaf is THE Čech Picard class of the datum's cocycle (stage (1e),
   158	consumed on the nose through `cechPicClass_eq_mk`). -/
   159	theorem sectionLocalEquations_picClass :
   160	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).picClass = D.cechPicClass := by
   161	  change Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒲
   162	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle.class = D.cechPicClass
   163	  rw [D.sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg]
   164	  exact D.cechPicClass_eq_mk 𝒲 σ hσ
   165	
   166	end AffineHom
   167	
   168	/-- **Independence of the section and the cover** (refinement/rescaling naturality,
   169	subsumed): the class of the divisor datum cut by ANY germ-regular section of the datum,
   170	on ANY subordinated pointed cover, is the same — both are `D.cechPicClass`. Unit
   171	rescalings and cover refinements of the constructed datum keep the class by the landed
   172	`LocalEquations.picClass_rescale`/`picClass_restrict`. -/
   173	theorem sectionLocalEquations_picClass_congr
   174	    {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
   175	    (s s' : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
   176	    (𝒲 𝒲' : (relCurve C B).PointedCover) (σ σ' : relCurve C B → D.index)
   177	    (hσ : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ y))
   178	    (hσ' : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲'.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ' y))
   179	    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
   180	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
   181	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y))
   182	    (hreg' : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
   183	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s' j)
   184	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y)) :
   185	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).picClass
   186	      = (D.sectionLocalEquations s' 𝒲' σ' hσ' hreg').picClass := by
   187	  rw [D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg,
   188	    D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s' 𝒲' σ' hσ' hreg']

   190	/-! ## The A2-bundled wrapper, on the canonical pointed cover -/
   191	
   192	section Bundled

   194	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
   195	variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
   196	
   197	/-- **Fibrewise-nonzero sections cut divisors** (DAT-A + DAT-A2, bundled): over a
   198	Noetherian test ring, a fibrewise-regular global section of the DAT-1 glued sheaf
   199	yields a `LocalEquations` divisor datum on the canonical pointed cover by pieces; its
   200	class is `D.cechPicClass` (`sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular_picClass`). -/
   201	noncomputable def sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular
   202	    [IsNoetherianRing B]
   203	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
   204	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
   205	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
   206	    (relCurve C B).LocalEquations :=
   207	  D.sectionLocalEquations s D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex (fun _ => le_rfl)
   208	    (fun j y hy => D.germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors s j (hfib j) y hy)
   209	
   210	/-- The class law for the A2-bundled wrapper: the fibrewise-regular section cuts a
   211	divisor of class exactly the datum's (1e) class. -/
   212	theorem sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular_picClass
   213	    [IsNoetherianRing B]
   214	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
   215	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
   216	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
   217	    (D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib).picClass = D.cechPicClass :=

150	/-! ## The collapse -/
   151	
   152	variable (C) in
   153	/-- **The chart twist is ONE θ-family** (this file's headline).
   154	
   155	`chartTwist C m Z T λ = λ · thetaFamily C (θ^m · (picClass k Z)⁻¹) T`.
   156	
   157	The Σ-shift and the `m` inverse θ-powers fuse into a single θ-family at the single class
   158	`θ^m · (picClass k Z)⁻¹`, which lives in `CechPic` over the FIXED base `overSpec k k` — a
   159	`CommGroup`, where the multiplication and inversion are free.
   160	
   161	Why this matters beyond tidiness: `w4-datc` §0.3 GAP-1 and `w4-datb` §1.6 both record that
   162	the twist "has no route" at the datum layer for want of a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.mul`.  The
   163	premise of that record is that the twist is a product of *families* which must be realised
   164	by a product of *data*.  It is not — it is one family, and the only multiplication happens
   165	in `CechPic` before any datum enters the picture. -/
   166	theorem chartTwist_collapse (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   167	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) :
   168	    chartTwist C m Z T lam
   169	      = lam * thetaFamily C
   170	          (thetaCechClass C ^ m * (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass k Z)⁻¹) T := by
   171	  rw [chartTwist, thetaFamily_mul, thetaFamily_inv, thetaFamily_pow, mul_assoc]
   172	  rfl
   173	
   174	variable (C) in
   175	/-- **The collapsed twist class**: the single `CechPic` class over the base that the chart
   176	index `(m, Z)` contributes.  Named because it is what a presenting datum must present, and
   177	because it makes the chart index's role visible — the whole twist is one class, and the
   178	chart-index degree constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − n` is a statement about *its* degree. -/
   179	def chartTwistClass (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) :
   180	    (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic :=
   181	  thetaCechClass C ^ m * (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass k Z)⁻¹
   182	
   183	variable (C) in
   184	theorem chartTwist_eq_mul_thetaFamily_chartTwistClass (m : ℕ)
   185	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   186	    (lam : picEt C T) :
   187	    chartTwist C m Z T lam = lam * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C m Z) T :=
   188	  chartTwist_collapse C m Z T lam
   189	
   190	/-! ## Presentation needs no GAP-1 mul
   191	
   192	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq` is a **surjectivity** statement: every Čech
   193	class over an affine base is the class of some datum.  So the datum the openness route needs
   194	is obtained by extraction *at the product class*, not by multiplying data.  The two lemmas
   195	below are one line each; they exist to make the point unmissable at the place a lane will
   196	look for it. -/
   197	
   198	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
   199	/-- **Extraction already presents any product or inverse of classes** — the general form.
   200	
   201	This is the direct refutation of "there is no `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.mul`, so a datum for a
   202	product has no route".  A datum for the product exists; what does not exist is a
   203	*construction of it from the factors' data*, which is a different (and unneeded) statement. -/
   204	theorem exists_datum_cechPicClass_mul_inv {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
   205	    (c c' : (relCurve C B).CechPic) :
   206	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π, D.cechPicClass = c * c'⁻¹ :=
   207	  BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq _
   208	
   209	/-- **A presenting datum for the collapsed twist class exists**, over any affine base and for
   210	any chart index — with no GAP-1 mul, no `invDatum`, and no `cechPicClass_inv`.
   211	
   212	`c` here is the honest Čech class of the plus class being tested (over the étale carrier,
   213	supplied by the collapse of `w4-datb` §1.2 step 1, i.e. `Pic0ChartSplit`), and the twist
   214	class is base-changed into `relCurve C B` along `relCurveMap`.  The conclusion is precisely
   215	the input of `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing`. -/
   216	theorem exists_datum_cechPicClass_chartTwistClass {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
   217	    (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) (m : ℕ)
   218	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) :
   219	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
   220	      D.cechPicClass
   221	        = c * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k B) (chartTwistClass C m Z) :=
   222	  BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq _
   223	
   224	end
   225	
   226	end AlgebraicGeometry

     8	/-!
     9	# A uniform pointwise section for the redesigned universal seed
    10	
    11	At a non-generic point of the residue-field fibre, the redesigned seed must use the
    12	landed base-divisor achiever.  At the generic point of a vertical fibre there is no
    13	closed-point achiever statement to apply; a nonzero compared window vector is enough,
    14	and its germ is a unit.
    15	
    16	This file makes that dichotomy into one vector-valued choice.  It records only the
    17	properties independent of the eventual basic-open cutter: membership in the universal
    18	first window, membership of the corresponding theta section in `divUniversalSeedK`,
    19	and nonvanishing after comparison with the residue field.  The local-principality/RD-N
    20	step can therefore choose its cutter later without reusing the older arbitrary seed
    21	section.
    22	-/

     9	# DAT-B B-5: the coverage obligation is Zariski-local in the test, so AFFINE tests suffice
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` reduced `ChartsCoverLocally` — and with it
    12	antecedent 2 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` — to pointwise data at **every test scheme
    13	`T`**.  That is where the reduction chain stops, and the quantifier it stops at is the
    14	problem this file addresses.
    15	
    16	**Every divisor-side producer in this project is indexed by a RING, not by a scheme.**
    17	`DivFamZar C S π n` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyZar.lean:235`) is a quotient of local-equation
    18	systems over an algebra `S`; `divFamZar C π n T` at a general test
    19	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyZarVehicle.lean:187`) is the affine-opens *limit* of those, and the
    20	comparison `divFamZarAffineEquiv` (:300) collapses it to `DivFamZar` only on an affine
    21	test.  Likewise every producer of a certified family, of an effective witness
    22	(`DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:147`), and every classifier
    23	(`effectiveDivisorClassifyZar`, :217) is stated over a ring or a field.  So a coverage
    24	lane facing "for every scheme `T`" has to cross the affine-to-general gap **before** it can
    25	use any of that machinery, and nothing said it was allowed to skip it.
    26	
    27	It is allowed to skip it, and that is this file's content.
    28	
    29	## Why locality in the test is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
    30	
    31	The naive argument — "sieves are local, so restrict to an affine cover" — is not available
    32	as stated, because `ChartsCoverLocally` is a statement about the sieve on `T` itself, and
    33	the pointwise hypothesis quantifies over points of `T`.  Three things have to be checked,
    34	and each is where the argument could fail:
    35	
    36	* **the class must restrict.**  The datum at a point `t` of an affine piece `Y` is about a
    37	  section over an open of `Y`, while the obligation at `t : ↥T` is about an open of `T`.
    38	  Composing `W.ι ≫ 𝒰.f j` gives a map into `T` but not an *open of* `T`, so the transport
    39	  cannot be done at the level of `T.Opens` — it has to be done at the level of the sieve,
    40	  where an arbitrary morphism is allowed;
    41	* **the sieve must be transitive.**  Membership of `⨆ i, imageSieve (f i) s` in the
    42	  topology on `T` is deduced from membership of its *pullbacks* along the cover maps, which
    43	  is `GrothendieckTopology.transitive` plus `Presheaf.pullback_imageSieve` — the latter is
    44	  what says the pullback of an image sieve is the image sieve of the restricted section,
    45	  i.e. that the obligation at `Y` is about `s|_Y` and nothing else;
    46	* **the pullback must commute with the supremum.**  `Sieve.pullback` is a left adjoint on
    47	  sieves, so it preserves `iSup`; without that the per-piece obligations would be about a
    48	  different sieve than the one the pullback of the target names.
    49	
    50	None of the three mentions `pic⁰`, a chart, or a divisor.  That is the point: the
    51	affine-to-general passage for antecedent 2 is a fact about the site, and mixing it with the
    52	geometry is what made it look like part of the geometry's price.
    53	
    54	## What this does and does not buy
    55	
    56	It buys the quantifier, and only the quantifier.  `chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` below
    57	asks for the pointwise datum **only over affine schemes**, and produces
    58	`ChartsCoverLocally` at every test; `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine` composes that
    59	with B-6.  So a producer may now assume its test is `Spec S` and reach for
    60	`divFamZarAffineEquiv`, `DivisorFamilyFieldSurj`, `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar` and the rest
    61	of the ring-indexed machinery directly.
    62	
    63	It does **not** produce the datum at an affine test.  That is B-5's geometry and it remains
    64	open; per `Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` and the `dat-b` row the residue there is
    65	the class-side question, and per `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean` the range containment `hV` is
    66	a further separate obligation.  What changes is that the residue is now stated where the
    67	tree's producers live.
    68	
    69	**On the converse, corrected.**  An earlier version of this paragraph said
    70	`affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally` makes the affine and general forms "equivalent", and cited
    71	that as discharging the `reduction-needs-its-converse` safeguard.  It does not: that
    72	declaration is `rfl`-equal to `pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally`, its `[IsAffine Y]` binder is
    73	never used, and the direction it certifies is the *free* one — general pointwise data gives the
    74	affine data by `fun Y _ s y => h Y s y`.  So the affine form is a genuine **weakening** of the
    75	general one, which is exactly why `chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` is worth having; the
    76	honest certificate is that theorem, not a no-op converse (audit `I-1023`).  The converse is
    77	kept only as the affine-test instance of the pointwise extraction, which is what it is.
    78	
    79	**On the atlas, and this is the sharper limit.**  Nothing here pins `V`.  The statements below
    80	take an arbitrary family `f`, which is what makes the site content reusable — but a consumer
    81	must supply coverage at the *same* `V` at which antecedent 1 was certified, and `ajcr-p1`
    82	measured both ends of that range to be bad: `hf` is free at `V = ⊥` (`isChartUniv_bot`, with a
    83	construction that never mentions the Abel chart), while `V = ⊤` returns the unrestricted
    84	certificate that three headers call false.  So any workable `V` is a proper intermediate open,
    85	CHART-U(b)'s openness is load-bearing, and the pair `(huniv V, hcov V)` has **no measured
    86	inhabitant at any `V`** (`I-1012`).  Two bad endpoints are two refutations, not a non-vacuity
    87	check.
    88	
    89	## Main declarations
    90	
    91	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine` — **the site fact**, with no
    92	  presheaf and no chart: a sieve on `T` is covering as soon as its pullback along every map
    93	  from an affine scheme in a cover of `T` is covering.
    94	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` — **the reduction**: pointwise
    95	  coverage over affine tests only gives `ChartsCoverLocally` at every test.
    96	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine` — the composite with B-6, i.e.
    97	  the instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, from affine-test data alone.
    98	* `AlgebraicGeometry.affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the converse, so the affine form
    99	  is not a strengthening.
   100	-/

   117	/-! ## The site fact -/
   118	
   119	/-- **A sieve is covering as soon as it is covering after pullback to affine pieces.**
   120	
   121	Stated for an arbitrary sieve on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses.  The
   122	cover is `Scheme.affineCover`, whose members are affine by
   123	`Scheme.isAffine_affineCover`, and the deduction is `GrothendieckTopology.transitive`
   124	against the presieve the cover generates.
   125	
   126	This is the step the coverage chain was missing: it says the Zariski-local-surjectivity
   127	obligation may be discharged one affine piece of the test at a time. -/
   128	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine {T : Scheme.{u}} (S : Sieve T)
   129	    (h : ∀ (j : T.affineCover.I₀), S.pullback (T.affineCover.f j) ∈
   130	      Scheme.zariskiTopology (T.affineCover.X j)) :
   131	    S ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
   132	  have hcov : (Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows T.affineCover.X T.affineCover.f))
   133	      ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T :=
   134	    Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr ⟨T.affineCover, Sieve.le_generate _⟩
   135	  refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.transitive hcov S ?_
   136	  rintro Y g ⟨V, a, b, ⟨j⟩, rfl⟩
   137	  rw [Sieve.pullback_comp]
   138	  exact Scheme.zariskiTopology.pullback_stable a (h j)
   139	
   140	/-! ## The reduction -/
   141	
   142	variable (C) in
   143	/-- **THE AFFINE-TEST REDUCTION**: pointwise coverage over affine tests gives
   144	`ChartsCoverLocally` at every test.
   145	
   146	The hypothesis is `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`'s, with `[IsAffine Y]` added and
   147	nothing else changed.  So a coverage producer may assume its test is affine — hence, through
   148	`divFamZarAffineEquiv`, that its divisor data lives over a *ring*, which is where every
   149	producer in this project is stated. -/
   150	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   151	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   152	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (y : ↥Y),
   153	      ∃ (W : Y.Opens) (_ : y ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   154	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   155	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
   156	  intro T s
   157	  refine mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine _ fun j => ?_
   158	  -- the pullback of the supremum is the supremum of the pullbacks, and each is the image
   159	  -- sieve of the RESTRICTED section — so the obligation at the affine piece is exactly the
   160	  -- affine instance of the hypothesis
   161	  have hpb : (⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i) s).pullback (T.affineCover.f j)
   162	      = ⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i)
   163	          ((pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (T.affineCover.f j).op s) := by
   164	    -- `Sieve.pullback` preserves `iSup` (it is a left adjoint), and per index it turns the
   165	    -- image sieve of `s` into that of `s` restricted along the cover map
   166	    simp only [← Presheaf.pullback_imageSieve]
   167	    ext Y g
   168	    simp only [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply, Sieve.pullback_apply]
   169	    aesop
   170	  rw [hpb]
   171	  -- the piece is affine (`Scheme.isAffine_affineCover`), so the hypothesis applies AT IT — note
   172	  -- `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` cannot be cited here, since it quantifies over all tests
   173	  -- and would demand the datum at the non-affine ones too; the site bridge is what is reused
   174	  choose W hW i x hx using h (T.affineCover.X j)
   175	    ((pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (T.affineCover.f j).op s)
   176	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun y => ⟨x y, hx y⟩
   177	
   178	variable (C) in
   179	/-- **B-5 over affine tests ⟹ B-6**: the local-surjectivity instance
   180	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, from affine-test coverage data alone. -/
   181	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   182	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   183	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (y : ↥Y),
   184	      ∃ (W : Y.Opens) (_ : y ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   185	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   186	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
   187	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal C f h)
   188	
   189	/-! ## The converse -/
   190	
   191	variable (C) in
   192	/-- **The affine form is not a strengthening**: `ChartsCoverLocally` gives back, over each
   193	affine test, a cover on whose members some chart hits the section.
   194	
   195	Read the carrier honestly, exactly as `pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` does: the sieve
   196	condition returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with open-immersion maps, not by opens of
   197	the test, so the converse produces a cover map where the hypothesis consumed an opens
   198	inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — that the affine-only hypothesis is available, not
   199	chosen for provability — a cover map is exactly as good. -/
   200	theorem affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   201	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   202	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y]
   203	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) :
   204	    ∃ (𝒰 : Y.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
   205	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
   206	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s :=
   207	  pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally C f h Y s
   208	
   209	end
   210	
   211	end AlgebraicGeometry

     8	/-!
     9	# A plus class becomes honest over its own étale carrier — over an ARBITRARY affine base
    10	
    11	This closes the obligation the CHART-U(b) header table names "honesty over a general affine
    12	base" (issue I-0558), and it needs no field.
    13	
    14	## The obligation, and why it looked hard
    15	
    16	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean`'s route needs a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over an affine base
    17	whose class is the (collapsed) twisted class.  `exists_datum_cechPicClass_chartTwistClass`
    18	(`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistCollapse.lean`) supplies the datum — but it takes an **honest Čech
    19	class** `c` over the base as a *hypothesis*, and a plus class over `Spec A` is not honest: it is
    20	`PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E` of `A`.
    21	
    22	The tree's only route from a plus class to an honest one was
    23	`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`'s `exists_splitting_of_picEt`, which requires `[Field K]` — its
    24	engine is étale field-cofinality (`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`),
    25	false over a general base.  So the obligation read as: find a *substitute* for cofinality over
    26	`Spec A`.
    27	
    28	## Why it is in fact free
    29	
    30	There is no substitute needed, because **a cover splits over its own carrier**.  The
    31	field-cofinality theorem is used to produce an `A`-algebra map `E.Carrier →ₐ L` into something
    32	where the class becomes a unit; but the identity `E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier` is already such a
    33	map, and it exists for every cover over every base.  Restricting the plus class along
    34	`A → E.Carrier` therefore makes it honest, with no finiteness, separability, or field
    35	hypothesis anywhere.
    36	
    37	Concretely `PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (PicEtAff.mk C E x) = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier x` — the
    38	transported class is presented by `x` itself.  The proof is the general-base analogue of
    39	`PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom` (`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:79`), which is stated
    40	only for fields; the field hypotheses there are inherited from *its* consumer (the degree seam,
    41	which reads a degree and so needs a field), not required by the argument.  The one substantive
    42	step is the same in both: the descent condition `x.2`, fed to `relPicAlgMap_congr`, identifies
    43	the two ways of transporting `x` to the base-changed carrier.
    44	
    45	## What this does and does not give
    46	
    47	It gives honesty **over `Spec E.Carrier`**, not over `Spec A`.  That is exactly what the
    48	(b-amendment) asks for — its step is "over the étale carrier `B := E.Carrier` the class is
    49	honest", after which the engine fires on `Spec B` and transport (ii) pushes the open locus down
    50	to `Spec A` along the (open, surjective) carrier map.  Nothing here performs that descent; the
    51	topological core of it is landed as `isOpen_of_isOpen_comap_preimage`
    52	(`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusOpen.lean:129`).
    53	
    54	So after this file the CHART-U(b) route has ONE remaining obligation, the pointwise
    55	`IsChartDatumPresentation` — and, unlike the previous "one remaining obligation" claims on this
    56	lane, that one is a genuine statement about matching two fibre predicates, not a missing
    57	construction.
    58	
    59	## Main declarations
    60	
    61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self` — **a plus class is honest over its own
    62	  cover carrier**, over an arbitrary affine base.
    63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_honest_of_picEtAff` — the existential form.
    64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_datum_cechPicClass_twist` — the payoff, in the engine's shape: over
    65	  a base where the class is honest, a datum presenting it twisted by any chart index exists.
    66	-/

    70	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

    93	/-! ## Honesty over the cover's own carrier -/
    94	
    95	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
    96	variable (C) in
    97	/-- **A plus class becomes the plus-unit of an honest class over its own cover carrier**, over
    98	an ARBITRARY affine base `A` — no field, no finiteness, no separability.
    99	
   100	`PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (PicEtAff.mk C E x) = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier x`: the class
   101	presented by `x` on the cover `E` restricts, along `A → E.Carrier`, to the tautological plus
   102	unit of `x` itself.
   103	
   104	This is the general-base analogue of `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom`
   105	(`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:79`) at `ℓ := AlgHom.id`.  That lemma carries `[Field K]`,
   106	`[Field L]` because *its* consumer (the degree seam) reads a degree; the argument itself uses
   107	neither.  The substantive content, identical in both, is the **descent condition** `x.2`: the
   108	two ways of carrying `x` into the base-changed carrier — along `E.baseChangeInclude` and along
   109	`Algebra.ofId` — agree on a descent class, which is what `relPicAlgMap_congr` consumes.

   111	Why this matters: the tree's only previous route from a plus class to an honest one was étale
   112	field-cofinality (`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`), which is field-only, so "honesty over a general
   113	affine base" was recorded as an unlanded *construction*.  It is not a construction at all — a
   114	cover splits over its own carrier, and the identity map is the splitting. -/
   115	theorem PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   116	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) :
   117	    PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (PicEtAff.mk C E x)
   118	      = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) := by
   119	  rw [PicEtAff.map_mk, PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk C (E.baseChange E.Carrier)]
   120	  refine congrArg (PicEtAff.mk C (E.baseChange E.Carrier)) (Subtype.ext ?_)
   121	  rw [descentBaseChange_coe]
   122	  exact relPicAlgMap_congr C (E.baseChangeInclude E.Carrier)
   123	    ((Algebra.ofId E.Carrier (E.baseChange E.Carrier).Carrier).restrictScalars A) x.2
   124	
   125	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
   126	variable (C) in
   127	/-- **Every plus class over an affine base is honest over some affine base above it** — the
   128	existential form of `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self`, which is how a consumer meets it: it does
   129	not get to choose `B`, it gets a `B` from the class's own presentation.
   130	
   131	Compare `exists_splitting_of_picEt` (`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`): that gives a *field*
   132	extension and requires the base to be a field; this gives an étale extension and requires
   133	nothing.  The two are the field and general-base halves of the same move, and the chart layer
   134	needs both — the field one to read the split witness predicate at a point, this one to run the
   135	engine over a base. -/
   136	theorem exists_honest_of_picEtAff {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   137	    (a : PicEtAff C A) :
   138	    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra k B) (_ : Algebra A B)
   139	        (_ : IsScalarTower k A B) (z : relPic C (overSpec k B)),
   140	      PicEtAff.map C B a = PicEtAff.unit C B z := by
   141	  induction a using PicEtAff.ind with
   142	  | mk E x =>
   143	    refine ⟨E.Carrier, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance,
   144	      (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)), ?_⟩
   145	    exact PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self C E x
   146	
   147	/-! ## The payoff: the engine's input, with honesty discharged -/
   148	
   149	variable (C π) in
   150	/-- **The engine input, assembled**: for any plus class over any affine base `A` and any chart
   151	index `(m, Z)`, once the class is read honestly over a base `B` above `A` by a Čech class `c`,
   152	a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `B` presenting `c` twisted by the chart index exists.
   153	
   154	This composes the two halves that were previously recorded as separate gates:
   155	
   156	* honesty over `B := E.Carrier` — `exists_honest_of_picEtAff` above, which needs no field;
   157	* presentation of the twisted class by a datum — `exists_cechPicClass_eq`, applied at the
   158	  *product* class, which is why no `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.mul` is needed
   159	  (`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistCollapse.lean`).
   160	
   161	The conclusion is exactly the input of
   162	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing`, so the openness of the witness
   163	locus over `Spec B` is available for every plus class and every chart index.  What is *not* here
   164	is the identification of that locus with `chartLocus` — that is `IsChartDatumPresentation`, the
   165	one genuine remaining obligation of CHART-U(b).
   166	
   167	Stated with `c` as a hypothesis rather than bundled into the existential: bundling it forces the
   168	elaborator to unify the tower instances on `B` while `B` is still a metavariable, which is the
   169	hazard recorded at `Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`'s closing note.  A consumer obtains `B` and `c`
   170	from `exists_honest_of_picEtAff` plus `relPicMk_surjective`, then applies this. -/
   171	theorem exists_datum_cechPicClass_twist {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
   172	    (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) (m : ℕ)
   173	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) :
   174	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
   175	      D.cechPicClass
   176	        = c * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k B) (chartTwistClass C m Z) :=
   177	  exists_datum_cechPicClass_chartTwistClass c m Z
   178	
   179	end
