     8	/-!
     9	# B-5 at the Abel chart: what the pointwise datum unfolds to, and what it costs
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` reduces `ChartsCoverLocally` — hence B-6 — to a
    12	four-part datum at each point of each test.  That reduction is stated for an *arbitrary*
    13	family of presheaf maps, so it says nothing about how hard the datum is at the family that
    14	matters.  This file instantiates it at `abelSigmaChart` and computes the answer.
    15	
    16	## The computation, and the one thing it makes visible
    17	
    18	A section of `pic0SigmaSheaf C` over a **bare** test scheme `T` is by definition a *pair*
    19	`⟨a, λ⟩` with `a : T ⟶ Spec k` and `λ` a degree-zero class on the slice object `Over.mk a`
    20	(`Over.sigmaExtension`, `Picard/OverSigmaExtension.lean`).  And `(Over.mk a).left` is `T`
    21	itself, definitionally.  So the big-site/slice crossing that looks like it needs a bridge does
    22	not: the pointwise datum's `t : ↥T` *is* a point of the slice test, and `chartLocus` applies to
    23	it with no transport.  `abelChartApp_eq` below records the crossing as an equation rather than
    24	leaving it to unfold at a use site.
    25	
    26	What the computation *does* make visible is where the cost sits.  `abelSigmaChart`'s value at
    27	`x : W ⟶ D.left` is `⟨x ≫ D.hom, chartValue … (rep.homEquiv …)⟩`, so matching it against the
    28	restriction of `⟨a, λ⟩` needs **both** components: the Σ-component is an equation between

    91	/-! ## The Abel chart's value, both components -/
    92	
    93	/-- **The Abel chart map evaluated at a point of the divisor scheme.**
    94	
    95	`abelSigmaChart` is `rep.toSigmaExtension ≫ Over.sigmaExtensionNat (chartValueTrans …)`, and
    96	both factors act componentwise on the Σ-extension, so the value at `x : Y ⟶ D.left` is the
    97	pair whose structure morphism is `x ≫ D.hom` and whose class is the chart value of the divisor
    98	family `rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)`.

   101	section, and the match is two equations rather than one: the Σ-components must agree before
   102	the classes are even in the same type.  Leaving it to unfold at the use site is how the
   103	Σ-component gets forgotten. -/
   104	@[simp]
   105	theorem abelChartApp_eq {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
   106	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)

   117	
   118	`chartLocusOpens` takes the affine-local openness as an argument.  Naming it is not cosmetic:
   119	an argument in a definition's signature is invisible to a census of open obligations, which is
   120	how "the `W` field costs zero" survived into two roadmap rows. -/

   122	variable (C) in
   123	/-- **The affine-local openness residue of `chartLocus`** — what `chartLocusOpens` costs.
   124	
   125	For a test `T` and a class `lam` on it, this says the chart locus is open over every affine
   126	open piece of `T`.  It is exactly the `haff` argument of `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'`,
   127	and it is the *only* remaining input to CHART-U(b) at a general test: the iso-invariance

   129	(`isSplitWitnessIsoInvariant_holds`), but this one was passed through, not proved.
   130	
   131	Named as a `Prop` so that it appears in searches for open obligations. -/
   132	def ChartLocusAffineLocal (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   133	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : Prop :=
   134	  ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
   135	    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))
   136	
   137	variable (C) in
   138	/-- `chartLocusOpens` with its cost made explicit in the API.
   139	
   140	Identical in content to `chartLocusOpens` — the point is that the dependency is now a named
   141	`Prop` a reader can grep for, rather than an unnamed argument that reads as bookkeeping. -/
   142	def chartLocusOpens' (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   143	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
   144	    (haff : ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam) : T.left.Opens :=
   145	  chartLocusOpens C m Z T lam haff
   146	
   147	@[simp]
   148	lemma mem_chartLocusOpens' {m : ℕ} {Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor}
   149	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} {haff : ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam}

   155	
   156	`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`'s docstring says the general-test statement follows from the
   157	affine one "by the affine-piece locality of the (b-amendment)'s transport (iii)", and adds that

   162	variable (C π) in
   163	/-- **The `haff` residue from a per-affine-piece presentation** — the link
   164	`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring describes and does not state.
   165	
   166	For each affine open `U` of the test, a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `Γ(T.left, U)` presenting

   168	(`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`), and `chartLocus` over the piece *is* that set

   170	twist commutes with restriction by `picEtMap_chartTwist`).

   172	So the affine-local residue is **exactly** B-4's presentation obligation, quantified over
   173	affine pieces — no extra geometry, and in particular nothing certificate- or divRep-gated.
   174	Combined with `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` this closes CHART-U(b) at a general test the
   175	moment `IsChartDatumPresentation` is available per piece.
   176	
   177	The `hπ` and `IsFinite π` hypotheses are the ones
   178	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` carries.  `IsFinite π` is strictly stronger than
   179	the file-level `IsAffineHom π` (whence the overlapping-instance warning, disabled below): the
   180	affine openness route runs through the rigid engine, which needs finiteness, while the rest of
   181	this file needs only affineness. -/
   182	theorem chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation [IsFinite π]
   183	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   184	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   185	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
   186	    (hpres : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
   187	      ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C (Γ(T.left, U.1)) π,
   188	        IsChartDatumPresentation C π
   189	          (chartTwist C m Z _ (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)) D) :
   190	    ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam := by
   191	  intro U
   192	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := hpres U
   193	  exact isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation C π hπ hD

   195	end

     9	/-!
    10	# DAT-B B-4 discharged at the admissible parameter: `ChartLocusAffineLocal` is UNCONDITIONAL
    11	
    12	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean` names the affine-local openness residue
    13	`ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam` — "the *only* remaining input to CHART-U(b) at a general
    14	test" (`Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean:127`) — and its only producers so far are **conditional**:
    15	`chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation` (`Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean:182`) asks for a
    16	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum` presentation per affine piece, and `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_plusFibre`
    17	(`Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean:128`) asks for a plus-fibre datum.  The obligation was priced by
    18	two roadmap rows and survived into the `chartLocusOpens` `haff` argument as an unexhibited cost.
    19	
    20	**It is free at the admissible parameter, for degree-zero classes, and this file says so as a
    21	theorem.**  `exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart_eq_univ`
    22	(`Pic0ChartCoverageThreshold.lean:381`) proves that at the parameter
    23	`m := admissibleCoverageParameter hπ g`, `Z := (…).choose`, the chart locus of **every**
    24	`pic⁰` class over **every** test is all of `Set.univ` — a set that is open by
    25	`isOpen_univ`.  `ChartLocusAffineLocal` asks for openness of the locus of the class *restricted*
    26	to each affine piece; by `pic0Map_coe` that restricted class `picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U)
    27	lam.1` is the carrier of the degree-zero class `pic0Map C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam`, to which
    28	`_eq_univ` applies again.  So the residue holds with no presentation, no plus-fibre, no arithmetic,
    29	and no `rep` — the numeric coverage result already contains the openness that CHART-U(b) needs.
    30	
    31	## Why this is the right carrier and does not overclaim
    32	
    33	`Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean:52-55` warns that `chartLocus` (on the *test*) and the
    34	open-immersion `V` (on the *divisor scheme*) do **not** meet, and that no tree declaration relates
    35	them.  This file respects that: it discharges only the *test-side* openness residue `haff`, which
    36	is exactly what `chartLocusOpens`/CHART-U(b) consumes; it does **not** touch antecedent 1
    37	(`IsChartUniv`/`RestrictedChartFibre`), the pointwise-to-neighbourhood spreading-out that
    38	`Pic0ChartCoverageSlice.lean` records as absent, or `rep`.  No antecedent of
    39	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` is closed here — one of B-4's two named inputs to CHART-U(b) is.
    40	
    41	## Main declarations
    42	
    43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusAffineLocal_admissible` — for the admissible parameter and any
    44	  degree-zero class, `ChartLocusAffineLocal` holds unconditionally.
    45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens_admissible_eq_top` — the open of the test that
    46	  `chartLocusOpens` produces from that residue is all of `T.left` (the locus is `univ`).
    47	-/

    57	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
    58	
    59	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    60	
    61	open AlgebraicJacobian
    62	
    63	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    64	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    65	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    66	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
    67	  [IsIntegral C.left]
    68	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
    69	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
    70	variable [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
    71	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
    72	
    73	noncomputable section
    74	
    75	/-- **DAT-B B-4 at the admissible parameter, unconditionally.**
    76	
    77	At the coverage chart index `(m, Z) := admissibleCoverageParameter hπ g` supplied by
    78	`exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart_eq_univ`, the affine-local openness residue
    79	`ChartLocusAffineLocal` holds for *every* degree-zero class `lam : pic0Subgroup C T` over *every*
    80	test `T`, with no presentation, plus-fibre, or arithmetic hypothesis: the chart locus of the
    81	restricted class is `Set.univ` and `univ` is open.
    82	
    83	This retires the `haff` argument of `chartLocusOpens`/CHART-U(b) at the parameter coverage
    84	actually uses.  The chart index `(m, Z)` is exactly the one `_eq_univ` produces (its `.choose`
    85	/`choose_spec.choose`); its own degree constraint is `_eq_univ`'s first conjunct
    86	`deg_k Z = m·d₁ − admissibleCoverageParameter` (note this subtracts `admissibleCoverageParameter
    87	= (M·δ+g)·d₁`, which carries the `d₁ = classDeg (thetaCechClass C)` factor — it is *not* the
    88	`(M·δ+g)`-without-`d₁` calibration some fixed-parameter chart data use, and neither theorem here
    89	depends on identifying the two). -/
    90	theorem chartLocusAffineLocal_admissible
    91	    {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
    92	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : ℕ)
    93	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    94	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
    95	    ChartLocusAffineLocal C
    96	      (exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart_eq_univ (C := C) hπ g hχ).choose
    97	      (exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart_eq_univ (C := C) hπ g hχ).choose_spec.choose
    98	      T lam.1 := by
    99	  -- the locus of the class restricted to each affine piece (`pic0Map`, `pic0Map_coe`) is all of

   101	  intro U
   102	  rw [← pic0Map_coe (C := C) (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam,
   103	    (exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart_eq_univ (C := C) hπ g hχ).choose_spec.choose_spec.2
   104	      (pic0Map C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)]
   105	  exact isOpen_univ

   108	`T.left`: the underlying locus is `Set.univ`. -/
   109	theorem chartLocusOpens_admissible_eq_top
   110	    {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
   111	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : ℕ)
   112	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
   113	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
   114	    chartLocusOpens C
   115	        (exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart_eq_univ (C := C) hπ g hχ).choose
   116	        (exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart_eq_univ (C := C) hπ g hχ).choose_spec.choose
   117	        T lam.1 (chartLocusAffineLocal_admissible hπ g hχ lam)
   118	      = ⊤ := by
   119	  apply TopologicalSpace.Opens.ext
   120	  change chartLocus C _ _ lam.1 = _
   121	  rw [(exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart_eq_univ (C := C) hπ g hχ).choose_spec.choose_spec.2

   123	  rfl

   125	end

     8	/-!
     9	# DAT-B B-6: the local-surjectivity half of the `(f, hf)` handoff
    10	
    11	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) needs two things beyond the
    12	charts: the `hf` certificate (C9b, reduced in `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`) and the
    13	instance
    14	
    15	```
    16	[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
    17	```
    18	
    19	which is dat-b row B-6.  Three files carry that instance as a `variable`
    20	(`JacobianDataCharts.lean:117`, `JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:183`,
    21	`JacobianDataAbelImage.lean:131`) and **nothing anywhere produces one**.  This file supplies
    22	the producer, in the form that DAT-B's coverage statement can actually feed.
    23	
    24	## What local surjectivity unfolds to, and why that matters here
    25	
    26	Mathlib's `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J f` has a single field: for every object `T` and
    27	every section `s` of the target at `T`, the *image sieve* of `s` — the sieve of maps
    28	`g : T' ⟶ T` along which `s` pulls back into the image of `f` — is a covering sieve.
    29	
    30	For the Zariski topology on schemes that is exactly the geometric statement dat-b row B-5
    31	proves: **every degree-zero class on a test is, locally on that test, a chart value**.  So
    32	B-6 is not a further geometric obligation on top of B-5 — it is B-5 phrased against
    33	mathlib's sieve-theoretic interface, plus the bookkeeping that turns a family of charts into
    34	`Sigma.desc`.
    35	
    36	The bookkeeping is what this file provides, and it is not trivial: the section must be hit
    37	by *some* chart of the family, and `Sigma.desc` must be shown to see it.  That is
    38	`ChartsCoverLocally` below.
    39	
    40	## The honest scope, stated up front
    41	
    42	`ChartsCoverLocally` is the hypothesis, not a theorem.  Its content is B-5 and B-5's residue
    43	is recorded on the dat-b roadmap row (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation).  What
    44	this file establishes is that **nothing else** stands between B-5 and the instance the
    45	producer needs — in particular no compatibility across charts, because `Sigma.desc` has
    46	none to check.
    47	
    48	## Main declarations
    49	
    50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartsCoverLocally` — the coverage hypothesis, stated exactly as the
    51	  image sieve of `Sigma.desc` being covering, but spelled in terms of the individual charts
    52	  so a producer never has to reason about the coproduct.
    53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` — **B-6**: that hypothesis gives the
    54	  instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
    55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective` — the degenerate sufficient
    56	  condition (a chart that is surjective on points of every test already covers), recorded so
    57	  the hypothesis is visibly *satisfiable* and not a disguised falsehood.
    58	-/
    59	
    60	set_option autoImplicit false
    61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    62	
    63	universe u
    64	
    65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    66	
    67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    68	
    69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    70	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    71	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    72	
    73	noncomputable section
    74	
    75	variable (C) in
    76	/-- **The coverage hypothesis of DAT-B, stated per chart rather than on the coproduct.**
    77	
    78	For every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the maps into `T` along which `s`
    79	becomes the value of *some* chart of the family form a Zariski covering sieve.
    80	
    81	This is dat-b row B-5 verbatim — "every `pic⁰` point is Zariski-locally a chart point" — with
    82	one deliberate design choice: the sieve is described through the individual `f i`, so a
    83	producer discharges it by exhibiting, for each point of `T`, one open neighbourhood and one
    84	index.  It never has to mention `Sigma.desc` or the coproduct of yoneda presheaves.  Turning
    85	that into the coproduct form is `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` below. -/
    86	def ChartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    87	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
    88	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)),
    89	    (⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i) s) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T
    90	
    91	/-- **B-6**: the coverage hypothesis gives the local-surjectivity instance that
    92	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
    93	
    94	The proof is the bookkeeping the row's name hides: the image sieve of `Sigma.desc f` contains
    95	the image sieve of every individual `f i` — because a `T'`-point of `X i` gives a `T'`-point

    11	
    12	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean:105` (`abelChartApp_eq`) records that the chart
    13	application is a **pair**, and its header warns that a coverage producer must match *two*
    14	equations rather than one — the Σ-components before the classes are even in the same type.
    15	Two roadmap rows and the c9b thread price the coverage datum accordingly.
    16	
    17	**This file first claimed that price was avoidable.  It is not, and the retraction is the
    18	content.**  The claim was: a producer working in the slice over `Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1)`, rather
    19	than handing over a bare `x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ D.left`, gets the Σ-equation as `Over.w` "for
    20	free".  What is true is that `Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ D` **is by definition** the pair of an
    21	`x` and a proof that `x ≫ D.hom = W.ι ≫ s.1`: `(Over.homMk x hx).left = x` and
    22	`Over.w (Over.homMk x hx) = hx` both hold by `rfl`, so the two hypotheses are interderivable
    23	and a producer can do nothing here it could not do before.  Refuted by a fresh-context audit
    24	(inbox `I-1021`); the durable lesson is `I-1024`.
    25	
    26	**The reusable error, since it is subtle.**  The non-vacuity check this file ran — `rfl` on
    27	`x ≫ D.hom = W.ι ≫ s.1` at unconstrained `x` **fails** — was read as licensing the discount.
    28	It forbids it.  An equation that is not definitionally free does not become free by moving
    29	into a binder's type; it merely stops appearing as a goal, which is what made the report
    30	convincing.  `slice_iff_bare` below is the one-line probe that settles such a question, and it
    31	is landed so the claim cannot be re-made here.

    33	## What this file is, honestly
    34	
    35	A **re-spelling** of the coverage datum, with the pair equation traded for one class equation
    36	plus a richer input type carrying the other.  `datum_of_slice` is one half of an equivalence
    37	(`bare_of_slice` is the other), so by the `I-0896` criterion no obligation was reduced.  It is
    38	worth keeping only because the slice spelling is the shape a divisor-side producer would want
    39	— every such producer here is stated over `overSpec k S`, so a route through them needs the
    40	identification of `Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1)` with `overSpec k Γ(Y, W)` at an affine `W`, and that
    41	identification is against the slice form, not the bare one.  That seam is not written here.
    42	
    43	The class equation is untouched and is the whole of what remains: it asks that the chart value
    44	of the divisor family named by `g` **is** the given class restricted.  Its cost is a divisor
    45	family over a *neighbourhood* produced from data at a *point* — a spreading-out, measured
    46	absent from the tree for this carrier by two independent censuses (every `DivFamZar` producer
    47	takes its base ring or the affine-opens limit first; the only spreading lemmas,

    53	**unrestricted** chart `abelSigmaChart`, whose source is all of `D.left`.
    54	`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54` and `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14` both hold that antecedent 1 is
    55	*false* there (the fibres are linear systems `|D|`, so it is not a monomorphism), while the

    10	/-!
    11	# Sections to divisors — the DAT-A2 germ-regularity bridge
    12	
    13	The geometry layer of the `lm:ctn` (iii)⟹(i) slicing criterion
    14	(`informal/spec-dat-a.md` §2; core: `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FibrewiseRegular`):
    15	
    16	* **(α) germ transport** — `IsAffineOpen.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors`: a nonzerodivisor of
    17	  the section ring of an affine open has nonzerodivisor germs at all of its points
    18	  (stalks are localizations of the affine section ring; regularity passes to
    19	  localizations). This is also the "germ-level regularity by localization-exactness"
    20	  consumption surface of DD-1a (dat-d-worksheet §1.2).
    21	* **(the field-level slice case, Kleiman tex 2013–2022)** —
    22	  `Scheme.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero`: on an **integral** scheme a nonzero
    23	  section has nonzerodivisor germs everywhere on its open. This is the named lemma
    24	  DAT-C discharges at field-level fibres ("nonzero on the integral fibre ⟹ regular").
    25	* **(β) piece flatness** — `flat_sections_basicOpen`: over `Spec k`, if the affine
    26	  chart ring is `k`-flat (`Scheme.overModule`) then so is every basic-open piece ring
    27	  (tower `k → Γ(V) → Γ(D(h))` through `IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen`).
    28	* **(γ) the generic A2 bridge** — `mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_fibrewise_regular` (+ germ
    29	  form): over a Noetherian `k`, a section of a basic-open piece of a `k`-flat affine
    30	  chart that is **fibrewise regular** (multiplication injective on every residue-field
    31	  fibre of the piece ring, in `Scheme.mulSectionEnd`/`rTensor` form) is a nonzerodivisor
    32	  with nonzerodivisor germs. The tensor-RING form of the fibre hypothesis converts
    33	  through `injective_rTensor_mulSectionEnd_of_tmul_mem_nonZeroDivisors`.
    34	* **(δ) A2 on the pinned datum** — for `D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` and a global
    35	  section `s` of the DAT-1 glued sheaf, each component `D.component s j` (the section on
    36	  the trivializing basic-open piece `D(h_j)`) is a nonzerodivisor with nonzerodivisor
    37	  germs, given its fibrewise regularity (`component_mem_nonZeroDivisors`,
    38	  `germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors`). These are exactly the `regular` inputs of
    39	  `Scheme.LocalEquations` — the LocalEquations construction and the class law are in
    40	  `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionsToDivisorsClass`.
    41	
    42	The fibrewise hypothesis is deliberately the *piece-ring residue-fibre* spelling
    43	(worksheet §2.2.2 with §5 risk 4 discharged): it is vacuous on pieces missing a fibre
    44	(zero ring), it is exactly what the integral-fibre slice case produces where the fibre
    45	ring is a domain, and it keeps the un-landed 1d-ii/DAT-3 fibre-sheaf identifications
    46	with their owners (DAT-C/DD-R bridge their fibre-curve statements to this spelling).
    47	-/

    61	section Bridges

    63	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]

    65	/-- A nonzerodivisor of a commutative ring is a regular element for the
    66	self-multiplication action. -/
    67	theorem isSMulRegular_self_of_mem_nonZeroDivisors {t : A}
    68	    (ht : t ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) : IsSMulRegular A t := by
    69	  intro u v huv
    70	  have h0 : (u - v) * t = 0 := by
    71	    have hm : t * u = t * v := huv
    72	    rw [sub_mul, mul_comm u, mul_comm v, hm, sub_self]
    73	  exact sub_eq_zero.mp ((mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff.mp ht).2 (u - v) h0)
    74	
    75	/-- A regular element for the self-multiplication action of a commutative ring is a
    76	nonzerodivisor. -/

    79	  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff]
    80	  refine ⟨fun z hz => ?_, fun z hz => ?_⟩
    81	  · refine h (show t • z = t • 0 by
    82	      rw [smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul, mul_zero]; exact hz)
    83	  · refine h (show t • z = t • 0 by
    84	      rw [smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul, mul_zero, mul_comm]; exact hz)
    85

    97	passes to localizations. -/

   102	    X.presheaf.algebra_section_stalk ⟨y, hy⟩
   103	  haveI := hU.isLocalization_stalk ⟨y, hy⟩

   112	nonzerodivisor germs at every point of its open. Named separately for DAT-C's canonical

   115	    {U : X.Opens} {t : Γ(X, U)} (ht : t ≠ 0) (y : X) (hy : y ∈ U) :
   116	    (X.presheaf.germ U y hy).hom t ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y) := by
   117	  refine mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero (fun h0 => ht ?_)

   130	/-- **Piece flatness**: if the section ring of an affine open `V` is a flat `k`-module
   131	(`Scheme.overModule`), then so is the section ring of every basic open `D(h) ⊆ V` —
   132	the tower `k → Γ(V) → Γ(D(h))` with `Γ(D(h))` a localization of `Γ(V)`.
   133	`private`: the public copy (same content, binder order `hV hflat f`) lives in
   134	`DivSchemeFamilySide` — same-day concurrent coinage (the I-0190 pattern), collision
   135	surfaced at the first full root build; external consumers use that copy. -/
   136	private theorem flat_sections_basicOpen {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (h : Γ(X, V))
   137	    (hflat : Module.Flat k Γ(X, V)) :
   138	    Module.Flat k Γ(X, X.basicOpen h) := by
   139	  letI : Algebra k Γ(X, V) := (X.overAlgebraMap k V).toAlgebra
   140	  letI : Algebra k Γ(X, X.basicOpen h) :=
   141	    (X.overAlgebraMap k (X.basicOpen h)).toAlgebra
   142	  haveI : IsLocalization.Away h Γ(X, X.basicOpen h) := hV.isLocalization_basicOpen h
   143	  haveI : Module.Flat Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen h) :=
   144	    IsLocalization.flat _ (Submonoid.powers h)
   145	  haveI : Module.Flat k Γ(X, V) := hflat
   146	  haveI : IsScalarTower k Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen h) :=
   147	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq'
   148	      (X.overAlgebraMap_naturality k (homOfLE (X.basicOpen_le h)).op).symm
   149	  exact Module.Flat.trans k Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen h)

   151	/-- **The generic A2 bridge** (`lm:ctn` (iii)⟹(i) on a basic-open piece of a flat
   152	affine chart): over a Noetherian `k`, a section `t` of `D(h) ⊆ V` whose multiplication
   153	endomorphism is injective on every residue-field fibre of the piece ring is a
   154	nonzerodivisor. -/
   155	theorem mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_fibrewise_regular [IsNoetherianRing k]
   156	    {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (h : Γ(X, V))
   157	    (hflat : Module.Flat k Γ(X, V)) (t : Γ(X, X.basicOpen h))
   158	    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum k, Function.Injective
   159	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd k t).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
   160	    t ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, X.basicOpen h) := by
   161	  haveI : Module.Flat k Γ(X, X.basicOpen h) := flat_sections_basicOpen k hV h hflat
   162	  have hinj : Function.Injective (Scheme.mulSectionEnd k t) :=
   163	    Module.Flat.injective_of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective
   164	      (Scheme.mulSectionEnd k t) hfib
   165	  refine mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isSMulRegular_self (fun u v huv => hinj ?_)
   166	  rw [Scheme.mulSectionEnd_apply, Scheme.mulSectionEnd_apply]
   167	  exact huv

   169	/-- The germ form of the generic A2 bridge: fibrewise-regular sections of basic-open
   170	pieces have nonzerodivisor germs (feeds `Scheme.LocalEquations.regular`). -/
   171	theorem germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_fibrewise_regular [IsNoetherianRing k]
   172	    {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (h : Γ(X, V))
   173	    (hflat : Module.Flat k Γ(X, V)) (t : Γ(X, X.basicOpen h))
   174	    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum k, Function.Injective
   175	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd k t).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   176	    (y : X) (hy : y ∈ X.basicOpen h) :
   177	    (X.presheaf.germ (X.basicOpen h) y hy).hom t
   178	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y) :=
   179	  (hV.basicOpen h).germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors
   180	    (mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_fibrewise_regular k hV h hflat t hfib) y hy
   181	
   182	/-- Conversion from the tensor-RING spelling of the fibre hypothesis (`t ⊗ 1` a
   183	nonzerodivisor of the piece-ring fibre `Γ(W) ⊗[k] κ(p)`) to the `rTensor` spelling the
   184	A2 bridge consumes. The `k`-algebra structure on the section ring is the structure
   185	morphism (`Scheme.overAlgebraMap`), whose module structure is `Scheme.overModule` on
   186	the nose. -/
   187	theorem injective_rTensor_mulSectionEnd_of_tmul_mem_nonZeroDivisors
   188	    {W : X.Opens} (t : Γ(X, W)) (p : PrimeSpectrum k)
   189	    (hfib : letI : Algebra k Γ(X, W) := (X.overAlgebraMap k W).toAlgebra
   190	      (t ⊗ₜ[k] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   191	          Γ(X, W) ⊗[k] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
   192	        nonZeroDivisors (Γ(X, W) ⊗[k] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
   193	    Function.Injective
   194	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd k t).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
   195	  letI : Algebra k Γ(X, W) := (X.overAlgebraMap k W).toAlgebra
   196	  have hend : Scheme.mulSectionEnd k t = LinearMap.mulLeft k t := by
   197	    ext s
   198	    simp [Scheme.mulSectionEnd_apply]
   199	  rw [hend, rTensor_mulLeft_eq_mulLeft_tmul p.asIdeal.ResidueField t]
   200	  intro u v huv
   201	  have hzero : (u - v) * (t ⊗ₜ[k] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) = 0 := by
   202	    rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply] at huv
   203	    rw [sub_mul, mul_comm u, mul_comm v, huv, sub_self]
   204	  exact sub_eq_zero.mp ((mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff.mp hfib).2 (u - v) hzero)
   205

   102	/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/
   103	
   104	variable (C) in
   105	/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.
   106	
   107	The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
   108	field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
   109	it, and every point `t` of `T`:
   110	
   111	* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
   112	  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
   113	  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
   114	* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
   115	  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
   116	* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
   117	  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
   118	* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.
   119	
   120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
   121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
   122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.
   123	
   124	**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
   125	and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
   126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
   127	written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
   128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
   131	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
   134	  intro T s
   135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
   136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩
   137	
   138	variable (C) in
   139	/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.
   140	
   141	The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
   142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
   143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
   144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
   145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
   148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
   151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)
   152	
   153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
   154	
   155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
   156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
   157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/
   158	
   159	variable (C) in
   160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
   161	
   162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
   163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
   164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
   165	
   166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
   167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
   168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
   169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
   170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
   171	pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
   172	exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
   173	theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   174	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   175	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
   176	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
   177	    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
   178	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
   179	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
   180	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
   181	  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
   182	  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
   183	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
   184	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
   185	  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩
   186	
   187	end

     8	/-!
     9	# At a one-point test, Zariski-local surjectivity IS surjectivity
    10	
    11	DAT-J's `quasiCompact` field reduces — in either coordinate system, see
    12	`Picard/JacobianDataQcFromRep.lean` and `Picard/Pic0AtlasCompactFromClass.lean` — to one
    13	statement `hcl`: **every point of the representing object has its class pulled back along some
    14	field point of the divisor scheme**.  Both of those files record that `hcl` has no producer,
    15	and the routes they name (the Abel image, finite-separable descent) are the expensive ones.
    16	
    17	This file supplies the general fact that reprices the *first* half of that statement, and it
    18	is not about `pic⁰` at all:
    19	
    20	> a Zariski covering sieve of a scheme whose space is a `Subsingleton` **contains the
    21	> identity**, so a locally surjective morphism of presheaves of types is honestly surjective
    22	> on sections there.
    23	
    24	`Spec K` for a field `K` is such a scheme (`Unique (PrimeSpectrum K)` in mathlib), and the
    25	tests `hcl` quantifies over are exactly `overSpec k κ(y)`.  So on the `hcl` side, coverage —
    26	antecedent 2 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`, which the seam **already assumes** — is not
    27	merely "locally" available at a field point: it gives a section on the nose, with no descent
    28	step and no Abel image.
    29	
    30	## Why the statement is about a `Subsingleton` space and not about fields
    31	
    32	The proof looks at the space only, and it goes through for an arbitrary presheaf of types on
    33	`Scheme`: take a cover refining the sieve (`exists_cover_of_mem_grothendieckTopology`), take
    34	the component over the unique point, observe its base map is epi *because the target has at
    35	most one point*, conclude it is an isomorphism (`IsOpenImmersion.isIso`), and use
    36	`Sieve.downward_closed` along its inverse.  Nothing here mentions `pic⁰`, the curve, the
    37	divisor scheme, or the sheaf condition.  Stated in that generality deliberately: it is the
    38	mirror image of `Picard/Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean`'s
    39	`not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot_of_presheaf`, which refutes the `V = ⊥` endpoint by
    40	looking only at the *emptiness* of the space.  Empty spaces kill local surjectivity; one-point
    41	spaces make it free.  Both are facts about the site, not about the Picard functor.
    42	
    43	## What this does NOT do, stated because the temptation here is exactly the audited failure mode
    44	
    45	**It does not discharge `hcl`, and it does not discharge any antecedent.**  What it gives is a
    46	section of the Σ-sheaf over `Spec κ(y)` *in the image of the atlas*, i.e. an index `i` and a
    47	`κ(y)`-point of the `i`-th chart source.  `hcl` asks for a point of `divSchemeOver …` whose
    48	class is `pic0Map C q lam` for the **one fixed** class `lam`.  Two gaps remain and neither is
    49	touched here:
    50	
    51	* the chart source of `mixedParamChart` is `(V i : Scheme)`, an *open of* `(D i).left`, and the
    52	  chart index `i` produced is the one coverage happens to supply — so the point obtained lies in
    53	  a chart of the atlas, not in a single named divisor scheme;
    54	* `hcl`'s `lam` is fixed *before* `y` is quantified, whereas coverage's index varies with the
    55	  point.  Collapsing that quantifier order is the real content of `hcl`, and this file leaves
    56	  it open.
    57	
    58	So the honest reading is: **the "local" in DAT-B's local surjectivity costs nothing at the
    59	tests DAT-J quantifies over.**  That is a subtraction from `hcl`'s price, not a payment of it.
    60	
    61	## Main declarations
    62	
    63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isIso_of_mem_zariskiTopology` — a covering sieve of a
    64	  `Subsingleton`-space scheme contains an isomorphism.  The only geometric input.
    65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.id_mem_of_mem_zariskiTopology` — hence it contains the identity, i.e. it
    66	  is the top sieve on the nose.
    67	* `AlgebraicGeometry.app_surjective_of_isLocallySurjective_of_subsingleton` — hence local
    68	  surjectivity of an arbitrary morphism of presheaves of types is surjectivity on sections
    69	  there.
    70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_chart_section_of_chartsCoverLocally_of_subsingleton` — the `pic⁰`
    71	  reading: at a one-point test, a covering chart family hits **every** section, by a genuine
    72	  index and a genuine point of that chart's source.
    73	-/
    74	
    75	set_option autoImplicit false
    76	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    77	
    78	universe u v
    79	
    80	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    81	
    82	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    83	
    84	/-! ## The site fact -/
    85	
    86	/-- **A Zariski covering sieve of a scheme with at most one point contains an isomorphism.**
    87	
    88	Take a cover refining the sieve; its component over the point `x` is an open immersion whose
    89	base map is surjective *because the target is a subsingleton*, hence an isomorphism.
    90	
    91	The `Subsingleton` hypothesis is on the space, and `x` witnesses that it is also nonempty —
    92	both are needed: on the empty scheme the bottom sieve covers
    93	(`Scheme.bot_mem_grothendieckTopology`) and contains no isomorphism at all. -/
    94	theorem exists_isIso_of_mem_zariskiTopology {X : Scheme.{u}} [Subsingleton (X : Type u)]
    95	    (x : X) (S : Sieve X) (hS : S ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology X) :
    96	    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ X), S.arrows g ∧ IsIso g := by
    97	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_grothendieckTopology hS
    98	  obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝒰.exists_eq x
    99	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (𝒰.f i) := 𝒰.map_prop i
   100	  haveI : Epi (𝒰.f i).base := by
   101	    rw [TopCat.epi_iff_surjective]
   102	    exact fun z => ⟨y, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩
   103	  exact ⟨𝒰.X i, 𝒰.f i, hle _ _ (Presieve.ofArrows.mk i), IsOpenImmersion.isIso (𝒰.f i)⟩
   104	
   105	/-- **A Zariski covering sieve of a scheme with at most one point contains the identity** —
   106	so on such a scheme "covering" carries no information beyond nonemptiness.
   107	
   108	`Sieve.downward_closed` along the inverse of the isomorphism above. -/
   109	theorem id_mem_of_mem_zariskiTopology {X : Scheme.{u}} [Subsingleton (X : Type u)]
   110	    (x : X) (S : Sieve X) (hS : S ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology X) :
   111	    S.arrows (𝟙 X) := by
   112	  obtain ⟨Y, g, hg, hiso⟩ := exists_isIso_of_mem_zariskiTopology x S hS
   113	  have h := S.downward_closed hg (inv g)
   114	  rwa [IsIso.inv_hom_id] at h
   115	
   116	/-- **Zariski-local surjectivity IS surjectivity at a one-point test.**
   117	
   118	For an arbitrary morphism of presheaves of types on `Scheme`: the image sieve of a section is
   119	covering by hypothesis, hence contains the identity by the previous theorem, and an identity in
   120	the image sieve *is* a preimage of the section.
   121	
   122	No `pic⁰`, no curve, no sheaf condition — this is the counterpart of
   123	`not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot_of_presheaf`
   124	(`Picard/Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean`), which refutes local surjectivity on the *empty* space by
   125	the same kind of purely site-level argument. -/
   126	theorem app_surjective_of_isLocallySurjective_of_subsingleton
   127	    {F G : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} (φ : F ⟶ G)
   128	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology φ]
   129	    {X : Scheme.{u}} [Subsingleton (X : Type u)] (x : X) :
   130	    Function.Surjective (φ.app (op X)) := by
   131	  intro s
   132	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ :=
   133	    id_mem_of_mem_zariskiTopology x _
   134	      (Presheaf.imageSieve_mem Scheme.zariskiTopology φ s)
   135	  exact ⟨t, by simpa using ht⟩
   136	
   137	/-! ## The instances at `Spec` of a field
   138	
   139	Recorded as `example`s rather than restated: both are mathlib instances
   140	(`PrimeSpectrum.instUnique` for a field), and the point of listing them is that the tests
   141	`hcl` quantifies over — `overSpec k κ(y)` — satisfy the hypotheses above with nothing to
   142	prove. -/
   143	
   144	section Field
   145	
   146	variable (K : Type u) [Field K]
   147	
   148	example : Subsingleton (Spec (CommRingCat.of K) : Type u) := inferInstance
   149	
   150	example : Nonempty (Spec (CommRingCat.of K) : Type u) := inferInstance

   152	end Field

   154	/-! ## The `pic⁰` reading -/
   155	
   156	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   157	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   158	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   159	
   160	/-- **At a one-point test, a covering chart family hits every section on the nose.**
   161	
   162	Given DAT-B's coverage (`ChartsCoverLocally`, the `pic⁰` spelling a producer actually attempts)
   163	and a test whose space has at most one point, every section `s` of the Σ-sheaf over that test
   164	is `f i` applied to a genuine point of the `i`-th chart source — no restriction to a
   165	neighbourhood, no refinement, no descent.
   166	
   167	This is what makes the "local" in B-5/B-6 free at the tests DAT-J's `hcl` quantifies over
   168	(`Picard/JacobianDataQcFromRep.lean`).  It does **not** produce `hcl`: the index `i` here is
   169	whichever one coverage supplies at `s`, while `hcl` fixes one class `lam` on one divisor scheme
   170	before quantifying over points.  See this file's module docstring for the two surviving gaps. -/
   171	theorem exists_chart_section_of_chartsCoverLocally_of_subsingleton {ι : Type u}
   172	    {X : ι → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   173	    (hcov : ChartsCoverLocally C f)
   174	    {T : Scheme.{u}} [Subsingleton (T : Type u)] (t : T)
   175	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
   176	    ∃ (i : ι) (x : T ⟶ X i), (f i).app (op T) x = s := by
   177	  have hid := id_mem_of_mem_zariskiTopology t _ (hcov T s)
   178	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hid
   179	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hid
   180	  exact ⟨i, x, by simpa using hx⟩
   181

    77	        𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y' ≤ 𝒲.opens y)).op).hom

     9	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ChiCurve
    10	
    11	/-!
    12	# DAT-C C2 — the rank-1 H⁰ export and the generator kit
    13	(`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` GAP-3 Σ-RANK1, §2 (N1)/(N3))
    14	
    15	On the fibrewise h¹-vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` with the base χ-normalization
    16	`χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`, the datum engine's `H⁰` is an **invertible** module: finite,
    17	projective, and of stalk-rank exactly `1`.  This is the rank export the engine
    18	(`datumRigidEngine`, `Cohomology/GluedSheafEngine.lean`) leaves open — it delivers
    19	finite + projective, never `rankAtStalk = 1`.
    20	
    21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_relCurve` — the χ transport `χ(𝒪_{C_L}) = 1 − n` to every
    22	  field `L` of the test tower (base-field invariance of the genus, `chi_moduleKSheaf`
    23	  + `genus_baseField`; a re-derivation of the private lemma of `DivSchemeMonoBridgeRel`).
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one` — **the fibre
    25	  computation**: for a datum whose fibre class over `L` has `classDeg = n`, with `H¹` of
    26	  the base-changed sheaf vanishing, `h⁰(C_L, F_{D_L}) = 1` — the Riemann–Roch anchor
    27	  `h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi` (`n + (1 − n)`) read through the presentation
    28	  bridge `presentationSheafIso`.  The fibre geometric package is threaded as instance
    29	  arguments (`Curve.BaseChangeInstances`).
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one` — **Σ-RANK1,
    31	  the datum-level export**: on the vanishing locus (fibre degree `n`, `χ = 1 − n`),
    32	  `Module.rankAtStalk (H⁰(F_D)) p = 1`.  Route: `Module.rankAtStalk_eq` reads the rank as
    33	  the `κ(p)`-fibre dimension; `datumH0BaseChange` (on the nose) identifies the fibre with
    34	  `H⁰(C_{κ(p)}, F_{D_{κ(p)}})`; the fibre computation above pins it at `1`.
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one` — the
    36	  certified-family specialization (**N1**): for `G` landing in the h¹-vanishing locus
    37	  `V`, the divisor datum `D_G := G.adaptation.divisorDatum` has invertible `H⁰`.  The
    38	  fibre-degree hypothesis is discharged uniformly by `DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass` (the
    39	  fibre class has `classDeg = n` at every field).
    40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily.exists_fibrewise_generator_divisorDatum`
    41	  — **N3, the generator kit**: since `H⁰(F_{D_G})` is projective of rank `1` (hence has a
    42	  nontrivial fibre at every prime of the locus), a fibrewise-nonzero **global** section
    43	  exists Zariski-locally (`Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`).
    44	
    45	Noetherian discipline (worksheet §2): every rank statement carries `[IsNoetherianRing S]`
    46	through the engine; the arbitrary-test consumers reach it through RE-5 stages.
    47	-/
    48	
    49	set_option autoImplicit false
    50	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
    51	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    52	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
    53	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    54	
    55	universe u
    56	
    57	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    58	open scoped TensorProduct
    59	
    60	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    61	
    62	open AlgebraicJacobian Scheme
    63	
    64	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    65	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    66	
    67	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    68	variable {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    69	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {n : ℕ}
    70	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    71	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    72	
    73	/-- The standing `C.left`-over-`k` structure, keyed on `C.hom` — the instance the base
    74	χ-normalization `hχ : χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n` is phrased against (defeq to `.ofHom C.hom`, so
    75	`chi_moduleKSheaf C` unifies with it). -/
    76	noncomputable local instance instOverCleftRankOne : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
    77	
    78	/-! ## The χ transport to the fibre curve -/
    79	
    80	/-- **`χ(𝒪) = 1 − n` at every field extension**, from the base normalization
    81	(`chi_moduleKSheaf` at the base-changed bundle + `genus_baseField`; a re-derivation of the
    82	`DivSchemeMonoBridgeRel` private lemma). -/
    83	theorem chi_relCurve (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
    84	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    85	    Sheaf.chi ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (n : ℤ) := by
    86	  haveI : IsProper (baseChangeBundle C L).hom := instIsProperSndLeft C L
    87	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (baseChangeBundle C L).hom :=
    88	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionSndLeft C L
    89	  haveI : GeometricallyIrreducible (baseChangeBundle C L).hom :=
    90	    instGeometricallyIrreducibleSndLeft C L
    91	  have h1 : Sheaf.chi ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L)
    92	      = 1 - (genus (baseChangeBundle C L) : ℤ) := chi_moduleKSheaf (baseChangeBundle C L)
    93	  have h2 : genus (baseChangeBundle C L) = genus C := genus_baseField C L
    94	  have h3 : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (genus C : ℤ) := chi_moduleKSheaf C
    95	  have h4 : (genus C : ℤ) = (n : ℤ) := by rw [h3] at hχ; linarith
    96	  rw [h1, h2, h4]
    97	
    98	/-! ## The fibre computation: `h⁰(C_L, F_{D_L}) = 1`
    99	
   100	The fibre geometric instances (`Curve.BaseChangeInstances`) are threaded as instance
   101	arguments — they cannot be synthesized through the `relCurve` `def` barrier, so consumers
   102	install them by `haveI` (the `degAt_abelDiv` block, I-0249 (iv)) before calling. -/
   103	
   104	/-- **The fibre h⁰ pin**: for a datum whose fibre class over the field `L` has
   105	`classDeg = n`, with the base χ-normalization and vanishing `H¹` of the base-changed
   106	sheaf, the fibre global-section count is exactly `1` — the Riemann–Roch rank anchor
   107	`h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi` read through the presentation bridge
   108	`presentationSheafIso`, at `n + (1 − n)`. -/
   109	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one
   110	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C S π)
   111	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   112	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra S L] [IsScalarTower k S L]
   113	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C L)]
   114	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
   115	    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
   116	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
   117	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
   118	    (hg : classDeg L (D.baseChange L).cechPicClass = (n : ℤ))
   119	    (hsub : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange L).sheaf 1)) :
   120	    Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf = 1 := by
   121	  set P : (relCurve C L).MeromorphicPresentation :=
   122	    Scheme.MeromorphicPresentation.ofCocycle (D.baseChange L).pointedCover
   123	      (gluedSubordCocycle (D.baseChange L).isGluingCocycle
   124	        (D.baseChange L).pointedCover (D.baseChange L).pieceIndex
   125	        fun _ => le_rfl) with hP
   126	  have hsubP : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (P.gluedSheaf L) 1) :=
   127	    (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv (presentationSheafIso (D.baseChange L)) 1).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mp
   128	      hsub
   129	  have h0eq : Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf = Sheaf.h0 (P.gluedSheaf L) :=
   130	    Sheaf.h0_congr (presentationSheafIso (D.baseChange L))
   131	  have hformula := h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi L P hsubP
   132	  have hPclass : P.picClass = (D.baseChange L).cechPicClass := rfl
   133	  have hint : (Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf : ℤ) = 1 := by
   134	    rw [h0eq, hformula, hPclass, hg, chi_relCurve hχ L]; ring
   135	  exact_mod_cast hint
   136	
   137	/-! ## Σ-RANK1: the rank-1 export on the vanishing locus -/
   138	
   139	/-- **Σ-RANK1, the datum-level rank export** (worksheet GAP-3): on the fibrewise
   140	h¹-vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` with the base χ-normalization `χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`,
   141	the datum engine's `H⁰` has stalk-rank exactly `1` at `p`.
   142	
   143	`Module.rankAtStalk_eq` reads the rank as the `κ(p)`-dimension of the fibre
   144	`κ(p) ⊗[S] H⁰`; the on-the-nose base change `datumH0BaseChange` identifies this fibre with
   145	`H⁰(C_{κ(p)}, F_{D_{κ(p)}})`, whose dimension is `1` by the fibre computation. The global
   146	fibrewise hypothesis `hfib` supplies finiteness/projectivity (hence flatness) through
   147	`datumRigidEngine`. -/
   148	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one
   149	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C S π) [IsNoetherianRing S]
   150	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   151	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   152	    (hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
   153	      Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   154	    (p : PrimeSpectrum S)
   155	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
   156	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   157	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   158	    [QuasiCompact
   159	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   160	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   161	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
   162	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   163	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)]
   164	    (hg : classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   165	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = (n : ℤ)) :
   166	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
   167	  obtain ⟨-, hfin, hproj⟩ := datumRigidEngine D hπ hfib
   168	  haveI := hfin
   169	  haveI := hproj
   170	  have hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1 := datum_subsingleton_pairH1 D hπ hfib
   171	  have hfibre : Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf = 1 :=
   172	    D.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one hχ p.asIdeal.ResidueField hg
   173	      (D.datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField hH1)
   174	  calc Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p
   175	      = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   176	          (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S] (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0)) :=
   177	        Module.rankAtStalk_eq p
   178	    _ = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   179	          (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf 0) :=
   180	        (D.datumH0BaseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField hH1).finrank_eq
   181	    _ = Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf := rfl
   182	    _ = 1 := hfibre
   183	
   184	/-! ## The certified-family specialization: N1 (invertible `H⁰`) and N3 (generators) -/
   185	
   186	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
   187	/-- (Implementation) The fibre class of the divisor datum has `classDeg = n` at `κ(p)`:
   188	the base change of `G.eqns`, read through `DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass`. -/
   189	private theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.classDeg_baseChange_divisorDatum
   190	    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) (p : PrimeSpectrum S)
   191	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
   192	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   193	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   194	    [QuasiCompact
   195	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   196	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   197	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
   198	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   199	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)] :
   200	    classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   201	      (G.adaptation.divisorDatum.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = (n : ℤ) := by
   202	  have hcl : G.adaptation.divisorDatum.cechPicClass = (DivFam.mk G).toZar.picClass := by
   203	    rw [G.adaptation.cechPicClass_divisorDatum, DivFamZar.picClass_toZar, DivFam.picClass_mk]
   204	  rw [G.adaptation.divisorDatum.cechPicClass_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField, hcl,
   205	    ← DivFamZar.picClass_mapAlg]
   206	  exact DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass
   207	    (DivFamZar.mapAlg p.asIdeal.ResidueField n (DivFam.mk G).toZar)
   208	
   209	/-- **N1 — invertibility of the canonical `H⁰`** (worksheet §2 (N1)): for a certified
   210	divisor family `G` landing in the h¹-vanishing locus `V` (`hvan`), the divisor datum
   211	`D_G := G.adaptation.divisorDatum` has `H⁰` of stalk-rank exactly `1` at every prime.
   212	
   213	The fibre-degree hypothesis of `rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one` is discharged uniformly:
   214	the fibre class of `D_G` at `κ(p)` is the base change of `G.eqns`, which has
   215	`classDeg = n` at every field (`DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass`). -/
   216	theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one
   217	    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) [IsNoetherianRing S]
   218	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   219	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   220	    (hvan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S, (DivFam.mk G).toZar.IsH1VanishingAt p)
   221	    (p : PrimeSpectrum S) :
   222	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
   223	  have hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
   224	      Subsingleton ((datumPair G.adaptation.divisorDatum).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   225	    fun q => (G.isH1VanishingAt_toZar_iff q).mp (hvan q)
   226	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   227	    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   228	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   229	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   230	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   231	  haveI : QuasiCompact
   232	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   233	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   234	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   235	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
   236	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   237	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   238	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=
   239	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   240	  exact G.adaptation.divisorDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one hπ hχ hfib p
   241	    (G.classDeg_baseChange_divisorDatum p)
   242	
   243	/-- **N3 — the generator kit** (worksheet §2 (N3)): since `H⁰(F_{D_G})` is projective of
   244	stalk-rank `1` on the locus, its `κ(p)`-fibre is nontrivial, so a fibrewise-nonzero
   245	**global** section exists on a basic open `D(f) ∋ p` — the Zariski-local generator
   246	(`Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`, the Nakayama-neighbourhood kit of
   247	`Picard/LocalGenerators.lean`). -/
   248	theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.exists_fibrewise_generator_divisorDatum
   249	    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) [IsNoetherianRing S]
   250	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   251	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   252	    (hvan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S, (DivFam.mk G).toZar.IsH1VanishingAt p)
   253	    (p : PrimeSpectrum S) :
   254	    ∃ f : S, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ ∃ q : Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0,
   255	      ∀ q' : PrimeSpectrum S, f ∉ q'.asIdeal →
   256	        (q ⊗ₜ (1 : q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   257	            Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0 ⊗[S] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0 := by
   258	  have hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
   259	      Subsingleton ((datumPair G.adaptation.divisorDatum).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   260	    fun q => (G.isH1VanishingAt_toZar_iff q).mp (hvan q)
   261	  obtain ⟨-, hfin, hproj⟩ := datumRigidEngine G.adaptation.divisorDatum hπ hfib
   262	  haveI := hfin
   263	  haveI := hproj
   264	  have hrank : Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) p = 1 :=
   265	    G.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one hπ hχ hvan p
   266	  -- rank 1 ⟹ the `κ(p)`-fibre is nontrivial
   267	  have hfr : Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   268	      (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S] Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) = 1 := by
   269	    rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_eq]; exact hrank
   270	  haveI : Nontrivial (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S]
   271	      Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) :=
   272	    Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos (by rw [hfr]; norm_num)
   273	  have hnt : Nontrivial (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0 ⊗[S]
   274	      p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   275	    (TensorProduct.comm S _ _).toEquiv.symm.nontrivial
   276	  exact Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective p hnt
   277
